News.title: College tutor wins the ‘Superbowl of bricklaying’ after laying 859 bricks in an HOUR to take home title
News.content:
A COLLEGE tutor has been crowned the king of British brickies after laying 859 bricks in just one hour.

Dale Wherton won the illustrious Super Trowel event, known as the “Super Bowl of bricklaying”.



He beat 15 other competitors to take home the title and will now take on other champion brickies in Las Vegas next year.

Dale, 35, said it was a “dream come true” to win Super Trowel 2026 at the Hertfordshire Showground in St Albans on August 1.



He got the competitive bricklaying bug at college in Stoke aged 15 before working in the industry for 20 years.

And he has honed his speed skills since becoming a lecturer six months ago at West Nottinghamshire College.

The dad-to-be, from Derby, said: “We have test walls with training mortar which doesn’t set, so we can put up and take down as many as we like.

“I remember 20 years ago my college tutor showed me this event in Vegas and I thought I’d really love to do that.

“Only one other Englishman has won it before as the Americans have dominated.

“Even the world’s best boxers dream of going to Las Vegas to compete. Now I’m doing it to lay bricks.”



Dale will compete in the Spec Mix Bricklayer 500 competition in January in the US.

He said: “I’ll be going there as an Englishman trying to win.”

News.title: Andy Burnham has insisted he will be ‘relentless’ in stopping small boats but latest booklet looks like a welcome pack
News.content:
Home truths

HARD-working Brits are being asked to believe that Labour is getting tough on illegal migration.

But the latest booklet being handed out to those arriving on small boats makes a mockery of that claim.



It encourages asylum seekers to quit taxpayer-funded accommodation and move in with friends or family who already live here.

They’ll be given help with their travel costs and will still receive £49.18 a week for food and essentials.



So what, exactly, is the deterrent?

Andy Burnham has insisted he will be “relentless” in stopping small boats. But this looks less like a crackdown and more like a welcome pack.



The message on the four-page leaflet is clear: Come to Britain, find a spare room and the taxpayer will help you get there. It is handed out alongside a nine-page guide on why raping or abusing women and children isn’t allowed.

Is the Home Office sure the recipients won’t just disappear and get a job in the black economy?

Labour insists the booklets are aimed at making British law clear to new arrivals and helping the drive to close more migrant hotels.

But yet again taxpayers are expected to shoulder the cost of mass illegal migration while ministers fail to come up with an effective deterrent to stop them arriving in the first place.



The PM has said he is “changing the whole approach” to dealing with the Channel crisis. He’s certainly done that.

It looks like he has simply given up.

Revise ideas

THOUSANDS of pupils were celebrating their GCSE results on Thursday — but many will have to go through it all again.

More than 350,000 youngsters face having to resit English or maths next year after failing to reach a crucial grade four.

It is vital that everyone hits the mark in these two important subjects if we are to stop today’s schoolkids joining the jobs scrapheap.



Education Secretary Lucy Powell must tackle low expectations in the classroom as a matter of urgency.

This will requires a fundamental reform of maths and English teaching at secondary schools to support those who struggle to attain a reasonable grasp of the 3Rs.

Failure is not an option.

Battle of bottles

PUBS are already fighting for survival — now Labour is to pile on another hefty bill.

Despite paying for their own recycling, they could be charged again for getting rid of bottles because they are classed as household waste.



Publicans warn it will cost £50million a year — enough to fund 4,400 bar staff or buy 11million pints.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

When pubs are closing their doors, the last thing they need is another tax-like burden.

Give ’em a break!

News.title: Home Office ‘don’t rape’ leaflet proves leftie loons know danger of open borders – there’s a simple solution to stop it
News.content:
WELCOME to Britain! Please wipe your feet.

Here in Blighty, our borders are now open to anyone who wants to come here — but we do expect everyone to obey our rules and customs.



If you come to our shores, you will need to learn to queue quietly, say “sorry” when someone else bumps into you, moan ­incessantly about the weather and, if it’s not too much bother, would it be okay if you didn’t rape any women or children, or beat your wives?

While the rest of us might take it for granted that rape, paedophilia and ­domestic abuse are most definitely not an acceptable part and parcel of everyday life in the UK, apparently not everyone does.



Which is why the Home Office has just published a nine-page booklet telling ­illegal migrants arriving in Britain not to commit those crimes.

The document, entitled “Understanding behaviours and expectations in the UK: A guide for asylum seekers”, sets out exactly what those expectations are and is to be handed out to the thousands of Channel migrants, helpfully informing them that rape is a serious crime, as is sex with children under 16.



Sexual harassment in the street is also not allowed, and neither is beating your wife or stopping her from getting a job or studying or, indeed, ­leaving the house when she wants.

What’s so surprising is that the Home Office thought this was necessary.

After all, Government ministers have been at pains to tell us these boat arrivals are desperate asylum seekers fleeing persecution — many of them women and children — not potential ­predators.

And people who have ­protested against these migrants being housed in hotels, bedsits or ex-Army ­barracks in their local areas have been branded racist bigots for ­claiming their new neighbours might be making their streets unsafe.



The Home Office booklet is basically a confession by the Government that they KNOW that some Channel migrants are a clear and present danger to women and children in our country.

Yet they continue to welcome them in their thousands to our shores, with a Channel taxi service, free accommodation and food, and legal aid to fight for the right to stay here.

For the ranks of liberal leftie lanyard loons at the Home Office, sitting on ­Commons benches, in the courts and working in migrant NGOs and charities, the rising tide of rapes, sexual assaults and sexual harassment on our streets is just a small price to pay for the pleasure of living in a NICE country that opens its doors to the world’s desperate hordes.



They simply refuse to face up to the reality that not all cultures are equal and that the whole world doesn’t sign up to Western values of equality and freedom.

Indeed, most of the world doesn’t — and particularly not in countries like ­Afghanistan, Eritrea, Iran, Iraq, Sudan and Somalia, where most asylum seekers are now arriving from.

Time after time, illegal migrants have been charged and convicted of raping and sexually assaulting women and girls, yet often the defence given in court is that they did not know what they were doing was a crime.

In one high-profile case, ­Ethiopian migrant Hadush Kebatu, 41, sexually assaulted a 14-year-old schoolgirl while he was living at the Bell asylum hotel in Epping, telling her that it is normal to marry children “in his country”.

And only this week, two Afghan migrant men, aged in their twenties, appeared in court accused of raping a 14-year-old girl on a London-bound train in February.



If only this booklet had been published before their alleged crime, eh?

How many more lives have to be ­sacrificed on the altar of the woke dogma that insists — against all the evidence — that it is a good idea to allow thousands of young men from medieval cultures into our country to roam our streets freely?

Even now, the Home Office is spending taxpayers’ money fighting a legal bid to force them to publish crime statistics by nationality, so they can continue to try to hide the true scale of the problem.

How many more British women and girls are expendable? How many rapes and sexual assaults will be enough to ­convince the Government that this is too high a price to pay? Because for most of us, ONE is too many.

Booklets and advice are not going to make our streets safer. Neither will ­sharing out the potential rapists “fairly” across the whole country, as the Home Office plans to do. (Out of interest, what do you reckon a “fair share” of ­foreign rapists in your local area would be?)



The solution is simple. Every single ­illegal arrival must be locked in a secure detention camp on Day One.

Their asylum applications must be assessed quickly, and those who fail to provide clear evidence for their claim must be immediately deported back home or anywhere else that will have them — Rwanda, Albania or a rocky outcrop in the middle of the ­Atlantic for all I care.

If the Home Office is so convinced that a booklet telling migrants not to rape will change how they behave, then let’s start handing out booklets on the beaches of Calais telling them it’s a crime to travel by dinghy to Britain. I’m sure it will work.

WHEN HARRY MET REALITY . . .

TALKING of the need for tougher border controls, two more economic migrants will be arriving on our shores soon.



Prince Harry and Meghan shocked the nation with their Megxit announcement in 2020 yet, just six years later, it seems their American dream is over and now we are getting the Great ReMeghration of the Sussexes to Blighty, with their tails between their legs.

It turns out life as Californian celebs isn’t quite as fun – or as lucrative – as they’d hoped. After selling every last ounce of their private lives to Netflix and Spotify and after telling the world every secret in their Oprah Winfrey interview and Harry’s memoir, Spare, there isn’t anything left to hawk.

And, frankly, sales of Meghan’s As Ever brand jam just aren’t going to pay the bills. It also turns out their only cachet was their royal link. Without it, they’ve quickly tumbled down from must-have A-listers to late-night TV show laughing stocks.

Maybe Harry wants to make amends with his family.

Maybe he’s bored. Perhaps he has finally sorted out his security concerns, or the couple think British schools will be better for their young children.



Or possibly they are leaving the US before Harry’s visa is cancelled over his drug-taking confessions. Who knows?

But I suspect what this is REALLY about is Meghan’s desire to see her children, Archie and Lilibet, with their HRH Prince and Princess titles, finally taking their rightful places on that Buckingham Palace balcony alongside the King and Queen, and William and Kate.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

It’s time for Meghan’s next reinvention as we tune in to see the Sussexes’ royal soap opera enter its latest season: The Non-Working Royals Return.

News.title: Flash floods and thunderstorms wreak havoc across Britain as water firms warn of hosepipe restrictions until Christmas
News.content:
BRITAIN was drenched by downpours as flash floods and thunderstorms wreaked havoc.

But water bosses warned the long-awaited deluge would do nothing to ease the worst drought for 50 years.



Thames Water said its hosepipe ban would likely last until at least the end of the year.

The nation’s largest water company serves more than ten million customers across London and the Thames Valley.



It said back-to-back heatwaves and barely a drop of rain for weeks had sparked an unprecedented surge in demand.

Its customers used around 100 million litres more water than normal each day during last month’s scorcher.



Boss Nevil Muncaster said the firm would have to extend current restrictions in order to “protect the environment”.

Other water firms are expected to make similar announcements in the coming days and weeks.

Mr Muncaster said: “The Environment Agency forecast is that it will be drier than normal for the next few months, but we’ll wait and see.

“At the same time, we’re going to make sure we protect the environment, make sure we see our ground flow and river flow restored.



“I think realistically it’s going to be towards the end of the year before that comes off.”

Thames Water is currently among 11 firms that have imposed hosepipe bans restricting more than 27million customers nationwide.

Yesterday’s rainfall was a welcome relief after the driest July since records began 190 years ago.



Vast swathes of the nation have been parched by the hot weather.

But racegoers at York’s Ebor Festival took shelter under brollies.

Cricket fans also took cover as the weather held up play on Day Two of the First Test against Pakistan at Headingley in Leeds.

Meanwhile, motorists on the M6 in Cumbria endured driving rain.

And shoppers and tourists at London’s Trafalgar Square hurried through showers.



Morecambe, Lancs, had more than two inches of rain in 24 hours.

The Met Office said it would be dry for most this weekend before a return to showers next week.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

The downpours arrived with three-quarters of England officially in drought.

Some places have gone without a drop for two months and July was southern England’s driest month on record.

News.title: Tragedy as girl, 5, dies after being ‘left in hot car outside home when family forgot she was there after school’
News.content:
HEAT HORROR Tragedy as girl, 5, dies after being ‘left in hot car outside home when family forgot she was there after school’

A YOUNG girl has been found dead after her family allegedly forgot about her and left the child in a boiling hot car.

Family members reported the five-year-old as missing before finding her unresponsive inside a car in Garland, Texas, police say.



Emergency services raced to the scene on Redbird Drive at around 8:20pm on Tuesday to find the youngster in a state of medical emergency.

Cops said the girl and her sibling had been picked up from school by an adult family member – her sibling got out, but the five-year-old did not.



The girl had just started school confirmed the local school district.

Family began searching for her – and then tragically found her still inside the car. Police say she could have been inside for hours.



CPR was performed and she was rushed to a local hospital – but tragically could not be saved.

Police have now launched an investigation into the child’s death.

“There are no words to describe how devastating this can be”, said Officer Matt Pesta, from the Garland Police Department.

He explained: “They started looking everywhere, right? Like you would a child, and then they started looking outside. Is she out there playing? You know, where’s she at? And then somebody located her still in the vehicle.”



No charges have yet been filed.

Counselling support has been offered to the family, police added.

Garland, Texas is currently under an extreme heat weather warning.



So far this year 23 children have died across the US in hot cars, according to data from the National Safety Council.

Last year a reported 34 children died in hot cars, including eight in Texas.

“The death is another wake up call for parents” Amber Rollins Executive Director of charity Kids and Car Safety told CBS.

“One of the biggest contributing factors to children being unknowingly left in vehicles is a shift in that normal daily routine. It doesn’t have to be anything huge.”

Chloe Burke, from the same charity, told KBTX: “Most of these cases are a mix of stress or fatigue, and then a change in routine. This is not a lapse of love. It’s just a lapse of memory, and you know, this could really happen to anyone.”



Breaking news… More to follow…

News.title: Afghan migrants ‘raped and assaulted girl, 14, on train after forcing her onto service’ bound for London
News.content:
TRAIN HORROR Afghan migrants ‘raped and assaulted girl, 14, on train after forcing her onto service’ bound for London

TWO Afghan migrants allegedly raped and assaulted a 14-year-old girl on a train after forcing her onto the London bound service, a court heard.

Baryalai Rahimi, 25, and Mirebadurahman Sadat, 29, are claimed to have carried out the attack on a South Western Railway service from Sturry to London Bridge in February.

The pair appeared at Inner London Crown Court today, Rahimi in a green shirt and Sadat in a grey jumper.

They were aided in court by Dari and Farsi interpreters, and spoke only to confirm their names.





Rahimi, of Southall in west London, is charged with three counts of rape, two counts of sexual assault, and assault by penetration.

Sadat, of Cricklewood in north west London, is charged with two counts of assault by penetration and two counts of causing or inciting a child to engage in sexual activity.

The pair have both denied all ten charges against them in court.

Following a brief hearing regarding the management of the case, Judge Michael Evans KC remanded Rahimi and Sadat in custody until November 4.

He told the defendants: “Defence counsel have taken a realistic position with custody time limits, I will extend it to 4 November.

“But there are a number of issues that have arisen, and that may cause adjustments to the timetable.”

Rahimi and Sadat will next appear at court on August 27 for further case management.

News.title: Asylum seekers encouraged to move in with friends & family in latest Home office booklet after ‘don’t rape’ leaflet
News.content:
ASYLUM seekers are being encouraged to move out of Home Office accommodation and stay with friends and family, The Sun can reveal.

A booklet handed out to new arrivals suggests they consider the move — and offers to cover travel costs.



But it raises fears that asylum seekers “can simply disappear” unless the system for monitoring their whereabouts is improved.

The Sun revealed on Thursday how another pamphlet in the series warned migrants not to rape.



The latest one reads: “You can stay with friends or family instead of in Home Office accommodation.

“It will not impact the outcome of your asylum application, and if eligible, you will still get weekly money for food and other essential items.”

The Home Office is under scrutiny over plans to move asylum seekers out of expensive hotels into old military camps — which can be even more costly.

As an incentive to leave its sites, the leaflet says: “We may be able to help with travel costs to your new accommodation.”

Sussex Police and Crime Commissioner Katy Bourne said the leaflet raises questions about how asylum seekers will be found once they leave Home Office sites.

She said: “The Home Office admits it has no mechanism for finding them, which is shocking.



“Unless we have a better system of monitoring their movements, they can simply disappear.”

Figures show 93,653 people are in taxpayer-funded asylum accommodation, including 20,885 in hotels.

Another 3,866 asylum seekers are receiving only subsistence support — meaning they have sourced their own housing — which is up 25 per cent in a year.

Asylum seekers can receive £49.18 a week to cover essentials such as food and toiletries while their claims are processed, but they cannot usually work.

Other booklets offered to new arrivals give advice on UK laws, such as telling them rape is illegal and the age of consent is 16.



PM Andy Burnham defended the leaflets, saying: “If you break UK law, you will be removed from the country.

“So it follows if we’re taking this approach, it’s made clear what the UK law is.”

A Home Office spokesperson said: “There’s been no change and Home Office accommodation continues to be provided only to those asylum seekers who have nowhere else to stay.

“We’ve cut costs by £1 billion since the general election and are determined to reduce the bill further.”

News.title: Hilarious moment Amazon delivery drone drops package directly into swimming pool as customer is left fuming
News.content:
THIS is the hilarious moment a delivery drone opens its hatch – and dumps its Amazon package directly into a swimming pool.

Lindsey Austen, from Texas, heard a loud buzzing sound and ran into her garden – only to be met with an astonishing sight.



Bizarre footage filmed by Lindsey shows the high-tech bot from Amazon’s Prime Air swooping into her back yard.

Bristling with six mini propellers, the drone artfully hovers over the pool – before suddenly unloading its contents from a height of around 30ft.



The cardboard box lands with a splash and can be seen bobbing in the water as the bot buzzes away.

“When it went into the pool, I was shocked,” Lindsey said, adding: “I don’t think I’ll be wanting any more drone deliveries.”

Shared by ABC7 News on Wednesday, the clip has since been seen thousands of times.

One viewer joked: “I love how it gently drops my package from over 30 feet in the air. Now that’s proper care.”

“Maybe she ordered a pool float”, another quipped.

The tech giant previously stressed that its drones deliver packages safely and quietly.



“Once the drone arrives at the preferred delivery point with a customer’s order, it will check to confirm there are no people, pets, or vehicles in the way before safely delivering the package”, said a spokesperson for Amazon.

It comes after another drone mishap in May where a bot dropped a package next to a pond where the force of landing sent it flying into the water.

Last year an Amazon delivery drone plopped a package next to a pool in Arizona – but the gusts of wind from the bot’s propellers blew the box into the water.



Amazon’s Prime Air service is still in its early phases – but the mega corp recently announced plans to expand to 500 new cities.

Some residents have already raised concerns about the disruptive sound of the delivery bots.

One Facebook user said: “Saw one just now outside my home. They’re louder than I was thinking they would be.”

Another commented: “I saw one yesterday flying over my neighborhood. It sounded like a small plane.”

Amazon has brushed off their complaints and said the sound level is comparable to an electric toothbrush.

News.title: Academic who accused Jason Arday of plagiarism ‘suspended’ from university
News.content:
Academic who accused Jason Arday of plagiarism ‘suspended’ from university

Nathan Cofnas, from the US, was also formerly employed at Cambridge University, from where Professor Arday resigned before his death

View 5 Images Nathan Cofnas is a self-confessed 'race realist' (Image: Adam Gerrard / Daily Express)

An academic who made plagiarism allegations against Professor Jason Arday before his death has been suspended by a university.

‌



Prof Arday resigned from his role at the University of Cambridge this month following intense scrutiny over accusations of plagiarism initially brought forward by Nathan Cofnas. Mr Cofnas, from Chicago, the US, is a postdoctoral researcher at Ghent University in Ghent, Belgium and was employed by Cambridge until 2024.

‌



Mr Cofnas said he has now been suspended from Ghent, and is under investigation for discriminating against Professor Arday. He has claimed he will "almost certainly" be fired from his position.

‌



View 5 Images Mr Cofnas says he will be sacked from his new position (Image: Adam Gerrard / Daily Express)

Announcing the news on X today, Mr Cofnas said: “I am under investigation by my university for discriminating against Arday.” He added in a second post: “I was just suspended by Ghent University. They will almost certainly fire me.”

Ghent University confirmed his suspension after saying in a statement that Professor Arday's death last week "should prompt reflection".

‌



A spokesperson said: “Ghent University formally notified the staff member concerned of the launch of a preliminary disciplinary investigation. As part of this process, the university is assessing whether there are sufficient grounds to refer the case to the competent disciplinary body for further consideration."

View 5 Images Professor Arday resigned from Cambridge following massive scrutiny into his work (Image: ARU)

"Pending this preliminary investigation, Ghent University has suspended the staff member as a precautionary measure.”

‌



The Belgian university said that while it supported academic freedom and open academic debate, “that freedom is not unlimited” and goes “hand in hand with responsibility” as it announced it was taking unspecified action regarding Mr Cofnas.

In a joint statement on Wednesday, Ghent University rector Petra De Sutter and vice-rector Herwig Reynaert said: “Ghent University stands for respect for human dignity and opposes discrimination, hatred and racism."

View 5 Images (Image: University of Cambridge / SWNS)

‌



“We attach great importance to academic freedom and to open academic debate, even when views are controversial. However, that freedom is not unlimited. It goes hand in hand with responsibility and may be restricted in order to protect the rights of others.

“For this reason, the university takes the recent public statements made by a postdoctoral researcher at Ghent University regarding this matter very seriously.

“Ghent University has decided to take appropriate action within its powers and the applicable framework.” The rector and vice-rector said that while it was “important to be transparent”, they did not want to “pre-empt any potential decisions at this stage”.

‌



View 5 Images Organusers said the Trafalgar Square vigil was attended by 30,000 people (Image: Tayfun Salci/ZUMA Press Wire/Shutterstock)

They said Ghent had been “shocked” by Prof Arday’s death and that their thoughts remain with his family, friends, colleagues and students.

Prof Arday, who became Cambridge’s youngest black professor in 2023, was found dead in Battersea, south London, on Friday. Earlier this week, organisers said more than 30,000 people had attended a vigil for the 41-year-old in Trafalgar Square, central London.

News.title: Fire engines race to meet easyJet flight in Manchester as pilot notices smell
News.content:
Fire engines race to meet easyJet flight in Manchester as pilot notices smell

Passengers were forced to disembark their easyJet flight to Turkey after the pilot reported smelling fumes in the cockpit, sparking a large emergency response

View 2 Images Fire crews surrounded the plane moments before take-off (Image: @pom0021/X)

Firefighters raced to an easyJet plane at Manchester Airport this evening after the pilot reported smelling fumes in the cockpit, forcing passengers to disembark moments before take-off.

‌



Holidaymakers were due to depart Manchester at 5:30pm before heading to Dalaman, Turkey on flight EZY 9143. But as the plane was being pushed back ready for take-off, the pilot reported the smell of fumes in the cockpit, reports Manchester Evening News.

‌



EasyJet confirmed the flight was cancelled following a "technical issue" and said emergency services, including airport fire crews, attended as "a precaution only".

‌



It is understood there was no fire affecting the Airbus A321, but passengers were disembarked and given hotel rooms for the night, with a replacement flight organised for tomorrow, the airline said.

View 2 Images Firefighters at Manchester Airport today (Image: @pom0021/X)

Burned bodies of lawyers found embracing in cockpit after hunt for missing plane READ MORE :

The emergency response is said to have briefly sparked delays for a number of other flights due to depart around the same time, but did not cause any major disruption.

‌



Around the same time, a fire alarm reportedly went off in the terminal, but this is believed to have been unrelated and a false alarm.

An easyJet spokesperson said: "Flight EZY9143 from Manchester to Dalaman was unable to operate on 20 August due to a technical issue with the aircraft. The aircraft was met by emergency services as a precaution only, and customers disembarked normally.

"Unfortunately, the technical issue meant the flight could not operate as planned.

Article continues below

"Customers have been provided with hotel accommodation and meals where required and are expected to continue their journey to Dalaman on Friday 21 August on a replacement aircraft.

"We are sorry for any inconvenience this will have caused and did all we could to minimise the impact of the disruption.

"The safety of our customers and crew is easyJet's highest priority, and easyJet operates its fleet of aircraft in strict compliance with all manufacturers' guidelines."

News.title: Peru struck by 6.7-mag earthquake felt in Ayacucho and Ica, causing landslides
News.content:
Peru struck by 6.7-mag earthquake felt in Ayacucho and Ica, causing landslides

A magnitude 6.7 earthquake hit Peru earlier today and caused landslides in the southern Andes Mountains - it was felt in several regions including Ayacucho, Ica and Arequipa

View Image The earthquake was centred 38km (24 miles) northwest of the city of Upahuacho (Image: US Geological Survey (USGS))

A magnitude 6.7 earthquake shook Peru's southern Andes Mountains on Thursday.

‌



According to the US Geological Survey (USGS), the quake occurred at 1pm local time (6pm UK time) and was centred 38km (24 miles) northwest of the city of Upahuacho, in the Parinacochas province of the Ayacucho region.

‌



There were no immediate reports of damage or injuries, and no tsunami warning has been issued.

‌



However, the quake has reportedly led to landslides in the area, with footage shared on social media showing locals in the streets looking up at debris falling down nearby mountainsides.

The earthquake had a depth of 66.7km and was felt in several regions of southern Peru, including Ica and Arequipa.

Content cannot be displayed without consent

‌



Earthquakes are frequent in Peru which is part of the Pacific "Ring of Fire", an area of frequent seismic activity.

In 2007, a magnitude 7.9 earthquake in a province of the Ica region left nearly 600 people dead.

It follows a major 7.4-mag earthquake in Colombia earlier this month which led to hundreds of deaths.

‌



President Abelardo de la Espriella has asked Donald Trump to suspend tariffs to help Colombia recover from the earthquake, which killed at least 289 people.

De la Espriella took office just days before the quake struck. He was backed by Trump in Colombia's closely contested presidential election, which was decided in a runoff on June 21, and has sought to emphasise his connections with the US leader.

On Saturday night, de la Espriella wrote on X that he spoke with Trump and thanked him for aid sent by the US in response to the earthquake.

Article continues below

He added that he "asked him to consider the temporary suspension of the high tariffs that affect Colombian products, in order to provide relief to our businesspeople, who are facing very difficult times due to the effects of the earthquake".

News.title: Wildlife killed in New Forest fire will take ‘decades to recover’
News.content:
Wildlife killed in New Forest fire will take ‘decades to recover’

Forestry England has warned that it will take years to remedy the ecological damage done to vast swathes of the New Forest ahead of a major transplantation project

View 5 Images A vast tract of New Forest was damaged during the wildfire (Image: Forestry England/AFP via Getty Images)

Wildlife and ancient trees destroyed in a horror wildfire the size of 140 football pitches will take decades to recover, experts warn.

‌



The fire, which ignited after a van caught alight on the A31 near Ringwood in the Hampshire district on August 9, grew to the size of 140 football pitches and took days for firefighters to quell. Hampshire Fire and Rescue deployed 26 fire engines and four water carriers to the scene following a major incident declaration, and crewmembers remain stationed on site to ensure the fire remains extinguished.

‌



With the fire largely halted, Forestry England has been able to conduct an initial assessment of the blaze's damage, and officials have concluded the site, which has high-level environmental conservation protections, could take many years to recover.

‌



UK weather maps show exact time violent thunderstorms and rain to batter nation READ MORE :

View 5 Images Firefighters remain on the scene to ensure the fire doesn't spread further (Image: Dorset & Wiltshire Fire and Rescue Service/AFP via Getty Images)

Forestry England said in a news release today that a specialist team was deployed to New Forest to map the area of the fire and analyse the damage caused. The blaze, the team found, has removed "all vegetation" from the area it scoured this month.

Among the areas it scoured, the organisation said, was precious heathland, where fragile and ecologically significant vegetation like heathers, gorse and pillwort, a rare plant found in the New Forest grow.

‌



The flames burned so deep that they also destroyed layers of seed banks under the soil, and a "significant number" of ancient beech and oak trees. They had been resident on the site for hundreds of years, and met a sad end after the fire tore into their root systems.

View 5 Images Both vegetation and wildlife were killed during the New Forest fire (Image: Forestry England/AFP via Getty Images)

Vegetation was not the only part of the fragile ecosystem that was destroyed, the organisation said, with bogs in the area, which are typically more heat-resistant than the local brush, also burned.

‌



They were partially destroyed by the heat, as were "a considerable number of wildfire", with Forestry England saying "so many" habitats were destroyed. Michael Pittock, Head of Planning and Environment at Forestry England said it was "devastating" to look at the damaged vitally important habitats.

He said: “It is devastating to walk around the area of the wildfire and see so much destruction especially on heathland which is such a rare and important habitat."

View 5 Images Among the destroyed foliage were ancient trees, which were burned down to their roots (Image: Getty Images)

‌



“A large area is damaged, but we are also very aware that without the remarkable response from the fire and emergency services it could have been so much worse. We are extremely grateful to them and all of the local partners and members of the community who have supported the New Forest during this difficult time.

“It will take decades for nature to fully recover but there are things we can do to help. Our teams will be working hard to support the area drawing on their experience of similar incidents and our ongoing restoration of heathlands across the New Forest.

"We will also be working closely with partners to support the recovery and build resilience across the Forest.” Thanks to the efforts of Forestry England, some of the local wildlife was recovered and moved to a neighbouring area.

‌



View 5 Images Satellite images showed the huge swathe of land burned by the New Forest wildfire

The organisation now plans to embark on what could be a lengthy process to restore the damaged area, which is nearby another part of New Forest that was damaged by a fire almost 40 years ago.

With that area having since been restored, it is planned to take cuttings from heather at the site to put together a protective layer that will help the soil recover and begin the reseeding process. Work is also ongoing on the A31, which was damaged when the lorry caught fire.

Article continues below

Those works are expected to continue into the weekend, and have seen authorities replace 1,500 metres of boundary fencing, road resurfacing and several hundred metres of vehicle restraint barrier.

A spokesperson for National Highways said the measures would be vital to ensure that animals don't enter the road, which could have safety ramifications for drivers. They said: “These measures are essential for safety reasons to deter animals from entering the road.”

News.title: 'Lion' spotted in Spanish tourist region as aircraft scrambled for massive hunt
News.content:
'Lion' spotted in Spanish tourist region as aircraft scrambled for massive hunt

The lion was allegedly spotted prowling in the mountains of Toledo, Spain, with a major search effort launched and locals warned to 'exercise extreme caution'

View 3 Images A massive search was launched for the animal (Image: Noticias CMM)

Helicopters and drones were scrambled in the mountains of a Spanish tourist region after a delivery driver claimed to have spotted a lion roaming in the area.

‌



The alleged sighting triggered a major response from authorities, with officers racing to hunt down the animal in the Toledo region in central Spain, which welcomes millions of tourists every year.

‌



The driver claims he saw the large feline at around 10:40am on Wednesday while travelling along the TO-1375 road near the historic Piélago convent in the Sierra de San Vicente.

‌



He immediately contacted the 112 emergency services, sparking a large-scale search by the Civil Guard.

View 3 Images Police at the scene in Toledo, central Spain (Image: Noticias CMM)

Body found after fire rips through factory as murder detectives launch investigation READ MORE :

Residents in nearby areas were urged to avoid secondary roads as officers tried to establish whether a lion was really on the loose.

‌



El Real de San Vicente Town Hall alerted locals on Facebook to a report "of a possible lion sighting near the convent in the mountains."

"There is no further information at this time; please exercise extreme caution," the post added on Thursday afternoon.

The emergency response included calls to local zoos, including one located around 15km from the reported sighting.

‌



Zoo Safari Fauna Aventura de Hinojosa de San Vicente said: "No animals are missing from our facilities," and threatened legal action over any claims suggesting an animal had escaped.

Checks of other zoos and wildlife reserves in the wider region, including nearby Madrid, also failed to uncover any missing lion.

View 3 Images Nearby residents were urged to 'exercise extreme caution' (Image: Noticias CMM)

‌



The mystery deepened as the search found no footprints or fresh sightings of the animal.

Officers also considered whether the driver could have mistaken a large dog for a lion, checking on owners' breeds including Tibetan mastiffs and German shepherds.

Authorities in Castilla-La Mancha meanwhile reminded the public that deliberately making a false report can be a criminal offence because of the emergency resources involved.

Article continues below

The search was eventually called off after "no evidence of a lion in the area" was found, according to sources at the Government Delegation.

It added that there have been no further sightings reported by the public since Wednesday morning.

The Civil Guard had been in touch with the affected town councils, as well as livestock farmers and the local population, "but these efforts have yielded no results."

News.title: 'Do not swim' warning at three UK beaches over 'contaminated water' fears
News.content:
'Do not swim' warning at three UK beaches over 'contaminated water' fears

Three beaches on the Isle of Wight have been closed to swimmers after rainfall resulted in 'outfall release that may have affected water quality', the Environment Agency warned

View Image The warning covers beaches at Gurnard, Isle of Wight (file) (Image: Getty Images/iStockphoto)

Swimmers have been warned to stay out of the sea at three popular UK beaches after rainfall triggered an "outfall release", sparking fears of contaminated water.

An alert has been issued by the Environment Agency for parts of the Isle of Wight following "an outfall release within the last 24 hours which may have affected water quality".

The warning covers beaches at Gurnard on the island's northern coast, as well as Shanklin and Bembridge to the east.

The Environment Agency is urging people not to enter the water in the affected areas, while the Isle of Wight Council has urged visitors "not to come into direct contact with contaminated water".

The council warned that sewage water " can contain bacteria and viruses that may cause illness".

UK weather maps shows 30C in 7 counties next week after Met Office 'hot' forecast READ MORE :

Met Office names areas facing heavy rain on Friday with downpours in 10 counties READ MORE :

Anyone who does come into contact with the water should " wash with soap and water" as hand sanitizer "does not kill all viruses which can cause illness".

Article continues below

Signs warning the public have been installed at the affected beaches, with a council spokesperson saying it had taken " immediate action to support public awareness and safety".

Details of the warning have also been shared online by the council and through Southern Water's River and Seas Watch website.

The alert has left some members of the public fuming, with one person describing the situation as an "utter disgrace".

One person commented: "This is disgusting. It cannot be from 'storm' drains."

A Facebook user added: " So so gross. Why is nothing being done about this!!?"

It comes after a number of pollution-related warnings have been issued around the Isle of Wight's coastline this summer.

Article continues below

Anyone requiring more information about the current warning can contact Environment Health on 01983823000.

News.title: UK weather maps show 30C in 7 counties next week after Met Office 'hot' forecast
News.content:
UK weather maps show 30C in 7 counties next week after Met Office 'hot' forecast

Some parts of the UK could see temperatures reaching 30C next week, weather forecasting models show, as the Met Office says 'hot' spells are on the cards

View 2 Images Anomaly maps show temperatures rising above the seasonal average in parts of England next week (Image: WXCHARTS)

Weather forecasting models suggest temperatures could rise into the high-20s and possibly even reach 30C again next week.

‌



The Met Office has said “short-lived warm or hot spells are possible” towards the end of this month and at the start of September, especially in southern regions.

‌



The GFS weather model now shows temperatures rising again from next Tuesday, reaching 26-27C in western England and Wales, before possibly peaking at 30C on Wednesday.

‌



The maps for Wednesday next week show the highest temperatures coming in eastern and south-eastern England where 29C-30C is on the cards, including in London.

In total, the data suggests seven counties could see 30C next week. They are all in England.

View 2 Images Maximum possible temperatures (C) at 6pm on Wednesday (Image: WXCHARTS)

‌



UK weather maps show new 34C heat surge with 15 counties reaching 31C or more READ MORE :

Met Office names areas facing heavy rain on Friday with downpours in 10 counties READ MORE :

UK counties facing 30C

Norfolk

Suffolk

Essex

Cambridgeshire

Hertfordshire

Middlesex

Kent

Met Office weather forecast

In its forecast for August 26 to September, the Met Office says that although temperatures are likely to be near the seasonal average, some warmer spells cannot be ruled out.

‌



The national weather agency predicts: “Becoming more unsettled and changeable from the south at the start of this period, as showers or longer spells of rain spread north across many parts of the UK. Some heavy bursts and thunderstorms are likely at times.

“Thereafter, it will likely remain changeable through the rest of August and into early September, with rainfall amounts probably above average for the time of year.

“Some drier, more settled interludes could develop at times. Temperatures are likely to be near average, although some short-lived warm or hot spells are possible, especially in the south.”

Article continues below

Looking further ahead in its forecast for September 4 to September 18, the Met Office says conditions “may turn warmer later with a chance of some hot periods in the south”.

However, the start of the period is likely to be “changeable” with “longer spells of rain across many areas, perhaps heavy and thundery in places”.

News.title: Harry and Meghan's return to UK reignites questions over security
News.content:
In terms of why they were moving now, a source close to the couple said the "stars had aligned" at this time to make the move work for their family.

They are described by the source as an international couple who love to travel - and for the next while they are going to be based in the UK.

As well as surprising the world's media, it was also news to King Charles, who was told about the move on Sunday. He is said to be looking forward to seeing them more often.

The decision follows a visit in July by Prince Harry, Meghan and their children to see the King at his Highgrove home in Gloucestershire.

It was the first time the King had seen his grandchildren in person in more than four years, and the couple's first visit to the UK together since 2022.

It has also been two-and-a-half years since the King was diagnosed with cancer and in Prince Harry's BBC interview last year, he spoke of wanting to spend more time with his father.

Highgrove has the feel of a family home rather than a royal palace - and royal author Valentine Low says a key driver of their return has been the chance for Harry to rebuild links to his family and particularly to "repair his relationship with his father".

The couple will still keep their California home and Meghan's work in the media and her online food business, As Ever, can be carried out from a base in the UK as readily as in the US.

Next year, Prince Harry's Invictus Games are being held in Birmingham, which would have meant extensive travelling to meetings and events in the UK.

It will also mark the 30th anniversary of the death of his mother, Princess Diana, which will bring commemorations and events in the UK.

This summer saw Prince Harry and his family staying at the Spencer family home at Althorp and returning to the UK will be a chance to be closer to his mother's side of his family.

News.title: Watch: What does Harry's return mean for his fractured relationship with William?
News.content:
The Duke and Duchess of Sussex, and their children, are planning on relocating back to the UK from the US later this month.

Prince Harry and Meghan left the UK and stepped back from royal duties in 2020, and family relations have been strained since.

The BBC understands that whilst King Charles III welcomes their return, he wasn't informed of it until Sunday.

There has been no official comment from his brother, the Prince of Wales.

The BBC's Helena Wilkinson looks back over the tumultuous relationship between the brothers and how Prince Harry's return may be received.

Read more here.

News.title: Five key takeaways from GCSE results day 2026
News.content:
You might be forgiven for glancing at this year's GCSE results and thinking not much has changed.

And sure, if you're just looking at the pass rate across England, Wales and Northern Ireland, that would be more or less correct.

But, when you dig into the detail, you'll find a more complicated picture, where some issues from last year have become even more stark.

You'll see the grades of students resitting their English and maths GCSEs in England are dragging down the overall results in those subjects - all part of a system the government itself says is "demoralising" and needs fixing.

You'll see that boys' and girls' grades are looking more similar - though that's more to do with girls slipping than boys improving.

And you'll see that, despite the government's pledges to "tackle entrenched inequality", the regional divide in England has actually grown, and remains stubbornly higher than it was before Covid.

Here are five key things you need to know.

News.title: French becoming more effective in stopping small boat crossings, UK says
News.content:
French police tactics are becoming more effective in stopping small boats in the English Channel from reaching Britain, the Home Office has said.

It credits French authorities with intercepting 185 potential crossings involving 4,300 migrants this summer over four separate weeks, as well as stopping 12 boats at sea using new techniques.

Footage released by French police shows officers racing across a beach in jeeps to intercept a launch. Once the boat is abandoned, an officer slashes it lengthways with a knife.

The Conservatives described the announcement as a "joke" and said Channel crossing preventions were "down by half over the past year".

Migrants can be seen throwing objects at the officers, one of whom appears to respond with pepper spray.

While Channel crossings are down about 40% compared to last year, thousands of illegal migrants are getting through with 250 arriving on Monday.

In late July a record 165 migrants reached the UK in a single boat with Border Security Command pictured towing a mega dinghy - estimated to be the same size as a standard bus at 13m (42ft) long - when it arrived in Dover on 23 July.

The Home Office, citing French police figures, said that since it struck a deal with France three months ago which included additional funding for authorities, 61% of small boats have been intercepted - a five per cent increase compared to last year.

Home Secretary Shabana Mahmood said the "UK-France deal is already having a real impact".

The UK-France Border Security deal agreed in April under the Starmer government, includes Â£501m over three years to strengthen operations in northern France and Â£161m for new approaches.

Previously the French authorities allowed most dinghies to head towards the UK once they had launched, because of the risk of intercepting them in deep water, while loaded with people.

Of the 12 dinghies stopped so far at sea, three interceptions took place in the last two weeks.

The techniques being used have not been disclosed by the UK or France.

Charlie Eastaugh, director of maritime and small boats at the Border Security Command, told the BBC that "last Thursday alone, the French prevented all three of the boats that tried to cross".

Speaking to the BBC at the Western Jetfoil facility in Dover used to process migrants, he said: "Two of those they prevented at sea, and one they prevented on land."

News.title: Academic who accused Jason Arday of plagiarism suspended by university
News.content:
An academic who accused the late Cambridge professor Jason Arday of plagiarism has been suspended from his post at a Belgian university.

Nathan Cofnas, a self-defined "race realist", was among those to question Arday's work and achievements - prompting a weeks-long plagiarism row prior to his death on 14 August.

Cofnas said he was under investigation by Ghent University "for discriminating against Arday".

The university said a staff member had been notified of a "preliminary disciplinary investigation" and suspended as a precaution.

In a statement regarding Arday's death, its rector Petra De Sutter and vice-rector Herwig Reynaert said they took "recent public statements made by a postdoctoral researcher at Ghent University regarding this matter very seriously", and had taken "appropriate action".

They said the university stood for "respect for human dignity and opposes discrimination, hatred and racism".

"We attach great importance to academic freedom and to open academic debate, even when views are controversial. However, that freedom is not unlimited.

"It goes hand in hand with responsibility and may be restricted in order to protect the rights of others."

They said Arday's death should "prompt reflection" and that lessons should be learned "regarding the way we treat one another both within and outside the academic world, particularly when people become the subject of public controversy".

Cofnas works as a postdoctoral researcher at the university's department of philosophy and moral sciences, according to his website.

His role at a Cambridge college was terminated in 2024 after backlash to his view that, under a true meritocracy, black people would "disappear from almost all high-profile positions outside of sports and entertainment".

News.title: John Swinney defends £45,000 business-class flights to World Cup
News.content:
John Swinney has defended the use of more than Â£45,000 of public funds on business-class flights for him and two senior aides to the World Cup.

Scotland's first minister flew to Boston on 11 June for Scotland's opening match, before taking part in trade talks in Kentucky three days later.

While he and two senior officials travelled business class, Sports Minister Maree Todd and several other officials went to the US on significantly cheaper economy-class flights.

Swinney insisted the government had sought to "minimise" costs, while Justice Secretary Neil Gray defended the business class flights as a means of ensuring ministers "arrive fresh" when they travel overseas.

In total, the government spent Â£98,442 on trips for Swinney, Todd and their officials to the US, including flights, hotels and expenses.

Flights for Swinney and his private secretary John Webster cost Â£17,893 each.

Business-class tickets for the first minister's special adviser Colin McAllister cost Â£9,864.

News.title: Belgian car salesman becomes prince after royal parentage confirmed
News.content:
Belgium's Prince Laurent has legally recognised 26-year-old former car salesman ClÃ©ment Vandenkerckhove as his son and heir.

Vandenkerckhove, the result of a relationship between the royal and Belgian singer Wendy Van Wanten, was quietly brought into Prince Laurent's family at a town hall ceremony six months ago, although details have only just emerged.

While he formally becomes a prince, he will not receive a royal allowance.

The new prince has had several years to get used to the idea of having a royal father, and he said recently he was not yet sure he would begin using his father's name Saxe-Coburg.

"I might want to do that, but I am proud of the name Vandenkerckhove," he told Het Nieuwsblad.

"If I were to sacrifice that family name, it would be a betrayal of everything my mother has done for me."

He will not be part of Belgium's royal line of succession, unlike his half-sister Princess Louise and half-brothers Prince Aymeric and Prince Nicolas. Nor will he take part in public royal activities.

Vandenkerckhove is already well known to Belgians, having been the focus of a Flemish TV documentary last September, in which he described how he got to know his father.

His father had been in a relationship with Wendy Van Wanten, whose real name is Iris Vandenkerckhove, before he went on to marry Princess Claire in 2003.

During the VTM documentary, ClÃ©ment described meeting the prince unexpectedly in a shopping centre in 2013, without realising who he was. It was only when he was 16 that his mother revealed his father's identity.

Four years later he plucked up the courage to ring him up, and after several more calls they met in person and eventually Prince Laurent suggested they take a DNA test.

"We went to the hospital together and I remember him saying 'I'll go first so you're feeling at ease'," he told VTM. Then he received an email from the laboratory which told him of a 99.5% DNA match.

Prince Laurent's DNA test is reminiscent of his father, former King Albert II, who had a test after a lengthy paternity battle. Albert admitted in 2020 that he had fathered a daughter during an affair and eventually recognised her as his own.

Albert II abdicated as king of the Belgians in 2013 as the paternity issue became a royal scandal.

Delphine BoÃ«l, a well-known artist, eventually won her court battle and gained the right to the title of princess, and now calls herself Delphine de Saxe-Coburg.

Under changes to Belgian law in 2013, only a few members of the royal family are entitled to public allowances - King Philippe, his father King Albert II, Prince Laurent and Princess Astrid.

News.title: BBC DJ Trevor Nelson reveals brain tumour surgery 'went well'
News.content:
BBC DJ and presenter Trevor Nelson has revealed he stepped away from work after being diagnosed with a brain tumour.

Nelson was last on air in June and had announced he was "taking a little break from my work commitments" due to "health issues".

Speaking to his Instagram followers, external, the 62-year-old said that his "world was turned upside down" when a brain tumour was discovered.

He said that he had undergone a "very serious surgery" which "went incredibly well".

Speaking on Instagram on Thursday, Nelson explained: "There's been a lot of speculation as to what's wrong with me, I know that much. My phone's blown up 20 times over with people asking what's wrong with me.

"I felt that I should at least tell you what was wrong with me. I'm not going to go into it all now and I will deep dive into it at a later date so you can hear the full story."

He continued: "I'll tell you this, I was minding my own business and then it was discovered I had a brain tumour.

"I was shocked, my world was turned upside down, it was a shock to myself and close family and friends and you can imagine quite literally my head was all over the place."

News.title: 'Relentless' GCSE resit cycle 'simply not working', school and college leaders say
News.content:
The "relentless" cycle of pupils in England failing and then resitting their GCSEs in maths and English is "simply not working", a leading education union has said.

The Association of School and College Leaders (ASCL) said a "significant proportion" of students fall short of passing those subjects, and that most who retake those exams "face the miserable experience of falling short once again".

Thursday's results data showed nearly one in four maths and English GCSEs in England were taken by students aged 17 and older, mostly young people resitting exams they had previously failed.

The government said it wanted to stop the "endless treadmill of unnecessary resits".

It said it would introduce a new "stepping stone" qualification from 2028 at Level 1 - one level below GCSEs - for students who do not achieve a pass in GCSE maths or English.

Currently, many courses and jobs remain dependent on students securing GCSE passes in those subjects.

But those that miss the grade can find themselves in a continuing loop of resits as they try and try again to pass.

Pepe Di'Iasio, general secretary of ASCL, said the fail-resit cycle was like "force feeding" students a "relentless diet of GCSE English and maths".

"This limits their education and career options and is very likely to be a factor in the large number of young people who end up not in employment, education or training," he said.

Pass rates for students aged 17 and older in English and maths are much lower than 16-year-old students taking the exams for the first time, bringing down overall GCSE grades for all ages across England, Wales and Northern Ireland as a result.

News.title: Man charged over Manchester synagogue attack
News.content:
A man has been charged in connection with the Manchester synagogue attack in which two men were killed.

Counter terrorism police said Hekmat Omar Ali Hakim, 49, of St James Road, Higher Broughton, Salford, had been charged with failing to disclose information regarding terrorist activity.

Hakim has been remanded into custody to appear before Westminster Magistrates' Court on Friday.

There have so far been eight arrests in connection with the attack, however this is the first charge that "relates directly" to the morning of 2 October, when two men died as the Heaton Park Hebrew Congregation synagogue was attacked by Jihad Al-Shamie. He was shot by police and died at the scene.

Worshippers Melvin Cravitz, 66, and Adrian Daulby, 53, were killed.

Assistant Chief Constable Rob Potts, from Counter Terrorism Policing North West (CTPNW) , said: "This is a significant development in our investigation, and my thoughts are with all those affected by the attack, particularly the bereaved loved ones and survivors.

"We have updated them and continue to offer them as much support as possible.

"Since the attack took place, we have been unwavering in our commitment to establishing the full picture behind the incident and identifying anybody who may have been involved in any way."

In July, Mohammad Bashir, 31, who planned an attack on a military base with the Manchester synagogue attacker was jailed for life with a minimum term of 17 years.

He drove his friend Jihad Al-Shamie on a 10-hour round trip to conduct hostile reconnaissance at the UK's Defence Academy in Shrivenham, Oxfordshire, on 14 August 2025.

Weeks after that journey, Al-Shamie, 35, was shot dead by police after carrying out the Heaton Park Synagogue attack.

News.title: People smuggler exposed by BBC investigation arrested and charged
News.content:
A convicted people smuggler who was found by the BBC to be living in Leicestershire has been arrested and charged with immigration offences.

Twana Jamal Khdir, an Iraqi national who was once described as "the godfather" of the French migrant camps, previously served a sentence for people smuggling in France.

Last month, the BBC revealed he was now living in the UK.

The BBC has been told he was arrested on Tuesday near Uppingham in a joint operation led by the Midlands Criminal Financial Investigations team, with the support of Leicestershire Police.

He was charged by the Crown Prosecution Service and appeared at Leicester Magistrates' Court on Wednesday.

He pleaded guilty to entering the UK without valid entry clearance, but not guilty to seeking to obtain leave to enter or remain by deceptive means.

He has been remanded in custody and will next appear at Leicester Crown Court on 5 October.

Khdir was given a five-year jail sentence in France in 2016, where authorities described him as one of the most successful people smugglers ever caught.

Prosecutors said the Iraqi Kurd, aged 36 at the time, had earned up to Â£100,000 a week for moving illegal immigrants across the Channel.

News.title: Thunderstorm warnings expire but rain continues to bring risk of floods for UK
News.content:
Heavy showers and thunderstorms will continue to affect large swathes of the UK on Thursday afternoon, bringing the threat of flooding and travel disruption.

A Met Office yellow thunderstorm covering parts of northern England and north Wales expired at 13:00 BST, with focus of heavy downpours shifting southwards across England and Wales.

Drivers are still being warned that wet weather could lead to slippery conditions and flooded roads.

The Environment Agency has issued one flood warning, external for Walverdon Water in Nelson, Lancashire.

Temperatures are also dropping with some places expected to remain below the August average over the next few days.

News.title: Vapes could lead to health harms in children, doctors warn
News.content:
Vaping could lead to health harms in children and young people and should be made "less attractive" to them, doctors have said.

The Royal College of Paediatrics and Child Health (RCPCH) has reviewed about 81 studies into vaping and said it is linked to higher rates of breathing problems and evidence of harm in babies whose mothers used vapes while pregnant.

The review said vaping should not be seen as a "harmless part of growing up".

The RCPCH is calling on the UK government to go further in its proposals to place new restrictions around the sale of vapes and suggests limiting the number of flavours that are available.

The review into vapes has been published in the journal Archives of Disease in Childhood. Experts from the college looked at the studies involving health or social outcomes of vaping on children and young people.

It said vaping had an association with problems including wheezing and coughing, poor oral and dental health, poor sleep, mental health problems and eye symptoms.

Co-author of the systematic review, Prof Will Carroll, said the evidence showed "clear links" with respiratory symptoms, nicotine dependence and subsequent cigarette smoking.

"We must act to make vaping less attractive and accessible to children," he said.

Vice-president for policy of the RCPCH, Dr Mike McKean, added: "Vaping is still a relatively new product, and there is much we do not yet know about its long-term impact on children and young people but a clear and concerning picture is emerging."

"We need to keep pace with a rapidly evolving market and continue to take action to protect children from nicotine products."

In July, the government launched a 12-week consultation on the appearance, packaging and display of vapes with the aim of reducing the appeal of the products to children.

As part of the new proposals, packs would need to be plain with strict limits on branding and only simple flavour descriptions like "apple" or "cola" used.

Other restrictions would move vapes out of sight in shops, similar to how cigarettes and tobacco are currently sold.

The 100-day consultation follows the recent passing of the Tobacco and Vapes Act,, external which sets out proposals to create the UK's first smoke-free generation.

Children aged 17 or younger now face a lifelong ban on buying cigarettes, since it will be illegal for shops to sell tobacco to anyone born after 1 January 2009.

Dr McKean said the new act was "an important step towards protecting children from nicotine addiction, but it must not be seen as a one-and-done solution".

Prof Carroll said the government needed "to go further and limit the types of flavours available to them as opposed to just their descriptions".

News.title: School 'deeply saddened' by death of family in sea off Shoreham
News.content:
A school attended by a 14-year-old girl who died alongside her father and mother after getting into difficulty in water off the coast of Shoreham-by-Sea has paid tribute to her.

Sara El-Khawas and her parents, husband and wife Hassan El-Khawas, 55, and Zeina Alayn, 37, are believed to have gone into the water near Shoreham Fort in West Sussex on Tuesday, according to Sussex Police.

In a statement on its website, the Ellen Wilkinson School for Girls in Ealing, west London, described Sara as a "sweet girl, well-liked by staff and students".

A fourth member of the family, a younger girl, remains in hospital in a critical condition, police confirmed on Thursday.

News.title: Burnham announces plans to clean up worst three illegal waste dumps
News.content:
Three of the country's worst illegal dumps are due to be cleaned up using taxpayers' money, the government has announced.

Sites in Kent, Surrey and West Yorkshire will be assessed for clearance, with Prime Minister Andy Burnham saying the "toxic dumps have blighted communities for too long".

Fines for waste offences will also rise from Â£300 to Â£5,000 to deter, catch, and punish those who dump illegally, and the Environment Agency will have more powers to seize assets bought with the proceeds of crime by those involved.

But opposition parties said illegal dumps were a small part of a much bigger issue with smaller scale fly-tipping and landfill all posing big problems for communities.

Burnham is looking to build on work started by his predecessor Sir Keir Starmer to tackle waste crime, with an action plan published in March detailing a series of measures - including using drones to map illegal waste sites.

Sir Keir's administration had announced that sites in Wigan, Sheffield and Lancashire would have government clean-ups - alongside Kidlington in Oxfordshire where removal of 20,000 tonnes of waste started in April.

The government said the new sites identified for clearance contain around 22,000 tonnes of illegally dumped waste.

They are: Power Station Road, on the Isle of Sheppey, Kent; Aymer Close, in Runnymede, Surrey; and Midland Road in Bradford, West Yorkshire.

West Yorkshire and Greater Manchester will be the first areas with new region-led approaches to waste crime.

The government said this will give mayors and council leaders the lead in co-ordinating councils, police, regulators, and other enforcement agencies.

Speaking on a visit to the waste dump in West Yorkshire, Burnham said: "We've begun a much more networked approach to this, where we're bringing the National Crime Agency in to work with the Environment Agency, increasing the penalties and bearing down now on the organised crime that lies behind some of what you see behind me."

The prime minister said the aim was to build intelligence about criminals linked to waste dumps at an earlier stage, to avoid the public being charged for clean-ups.

"We should be getting in much earlier, apprehending them, using all of the intelligence that comes through that investigation to make sure the polluter pays," he added.

A new "waste crime crackdown group", chaired by Environment Secretary Angela Eagle, will bring regulators and law enforcement together in a bid to dismantle criminal operations.

Eagle said: "We are cleaning up sites, but we are also stopping the cycle, driving faster prevention and disruption, better intelligence, and stronger coordination across the system."

News.title: Reform UK proposes tax rebates for firms to boost apprenticeships
News.content:
Young apprentices should have part of their wages paid by taxpayers, according to Reform UK plans, external aimed at delivering a "skills revolution".

The party's education spokeswoman Suella Braverman said a Reform government would introduce an "apprenticeship wage credit" offering small and medium-sized businesses a 30% rebate on the wages of apprentices they take on aged 16 to 18.

She also advised students receiving their GCSE exam results on Thursday "not to get ripped off by the great university scam" and to learn a trade instead.

Prime Minister Andy Burnham has said he wants teenagers to have technical routes into careers that could rival the path of a traditional university degree.

The government has been introducing changes and examining ways to encourage more young people into work, including giving some parents on benefits up to Â£4,500 a year to encourage their children to start apprenticeships.

Former minister Alan Milburn has been tasked with investigating why so many young people are not in employment, education or training - known by the acronym Neets.

Reform said its announcement was the first in a series of proposals aimed at reaching 600,000 apprenticeship starts per year by the end of the next Parliament, likely to be 2034.

The party says it would pay for its plans by banning all foreign students from accessing taxpayer-funded loans and stopping what the party calls "Mickey Mouse degrees".

Reform said its policy, which also includes a Â£2,000 retention bonus for apprentices, could cost between Â£1.48bn and almost Â£2bn over five years.

Braverman said there are "excessive number of graduates with qualifications that don't match the skills needed for our country," arguing that learning a trade would be a better use of their time.

Apprentices are generally paid a lower wage but get on-the-job training and practical work experience.

Speaking at a press conference, Braverman said: "We're firing the starting gun on unleashing a technical and vocational renaissance of homegrown skills.

"Reform will not do this because it fills us with some jingoistic pride but because we will do what it takes to save Britain from the perpetual doom loop of decline, debt and despair that we're currently in."

The MP said the apprenticeship wage credit would result in businesses saving an average of Â£4,000-a-year per apprentice.

The Â£2,000 tax-free retention bonus would be paid to workers who "show loyalty" by staying with the business that trained them for at least two years after they complete their apprenticeship, said Braverman.

Asked if the policy would mean some universities would have to close, Braverman said she did not envisage that but instead suggested universities need to "repurpose" themselves into construction colleges and manufacturing colleges.

When pressed to give examples of "Mickey Mouse degrees", Braverman pointed to "gender studies" and "golf course studies".

She said: "There's not a necessity, there's not a value in many of these degrees."

The British and International Golf Greenkeepers Association (BIGGA) has previously criticised Braverman for similar remarks, which they branded "negligent and potentially damaging".

BIGGA chief executive Jim Croxton said: "Golf course management is a growing industry with currently more vacancies than qualified applicants.

"Anyone successfully studying for a degree in this field is effectively guaranteed employment in a vibrant industry."

A Labour Party spokesperson said all young people "deserve a clear route to a good career" whether through "a properly funded apprenticeship, high-quality technical education or university".

The spokesperson added: "That's exactly what this Labour government is already delivering, with 500,000 new jobs, apprenticeships and training opportunities to help young people earn or learn, including a guaranteed job for 18â24-year-olds who have been out of work for 18 months."

On Wednesday, Conservative shadow education secretary Laura Trott said there is demand for apprenticeships but claimed the Labour government "aren't doing enough to boost supply".

She said: "Our New Deal for Young People would axe the dead end degrees that don't lead to jobs and instead invest in apprenticeships giving school leavers more choice."

Liberal Democrat universities spokesperson Ian Sollom said it was important to protect local colleges and universities as well as boosting apprenticeships, including apprenticeships in degree courses.

"Reform's proposals amount to dangerous economic vandalism which would rip a multi-billion-pound hole in our world-leading university sector," he added.

Green Party MP Hannah Spencer, who was a plumber before becoming an MP, said: "People are tired of Reform pitting us against each other - Those of us that did apprenticeships can still see the value in degrees and everyone should be able to choose their own path of education."

She added the Greens had announced a windfall tax on big banks, which she said would support small businesses employing more young people.
