Sports.title: TNT Sport bosses bemused by Joe Cole after pundit bizarrely claimed Hull City have arrived in the Premier League 'through the back door' and he snubbed call to cover opening game - as Tigers owner hits back
Sports.content:
Joe Cole has sparked a furious response from Hull City fans after claiming the Tigers are already relegated - and saying he put his phone on ‘do not disturb’ to ensure he would not have to be a pundit for TNT Sports at their season opener against Manchester United tomorrow night. The former Chelsea and England man has triggered outrage in East Yorkshire thanks to comments he made with former West Ham team-mate Carlton Cole on a podcast. When asked who would be going down this season, Cole said ‘Hull are gone, man’ before claiming that they had arrived in the Premier League ‘through the back door’. He then added that he had ‘a confession to make’, saying he had been contacted by TNT Sports who ‘tried to slip in Hull on the first day of the season’. ‘I put my phone on Do Not Disturb,’ he said. Hull City are GOING DOWN! 🗣️🐯 The lads don’t rate Hull’s chances this season 🥺 Watch in full 👉 https://t.co/PuonqV3D90#TheDressingRoom #PremierLeague #PL pic.twitter.com/B1xa8RV4nI — The Dressing Room Podcast (@dressingroomaa) August 19, 2026 Joe Cole has risked the wrath of Hull City fans with comments made on his podcast

Your browser does not support iframes.

Daily Mail Sport understands the comments have left bosses at TNT Sports bemused, with insiders saying Cole was not down to cover the opener at the MKM Stadium, and never had been. Regardless, it has stoked plenty of emotion in Hull. Sources have disclosed that players and staff are well aware of what was said and intend to use it as motivation for what would appear to be a tough mission ahead. Fans have taken to social media to highlight what they see as a ‘condescending’ and ‘disrespectful’ attitude, with some even claiming the newly-promoted club, who won the Championship play-off final, should ban Cole from its stadium. Hull owner Acun Ilicali responded to the comments from both Coles on social media, writing: 'It is disappointing to see my beautiful city criticised by people who should know better. 'As a club we are used to being underestimated and we enjoy it, and we enjoyed it more when were promoted last season. 'The true beauty of a place is in its people, and that’s why, for me, Hull is one of the most beautiful places in the world. 'For me, seeing two ex-players making fun of a deservedly promoted club, is more laughable than the things they were laughing at.'

Sports.title: Xabi Alonso refuses to rule out Enzo Fernandez exit with Chelsea set to demand MORE than £120m asking price for star man after Man City missed transfer deadline
Sports.content:
Xabi Alonso refused to guarantee that Enzo Fernandez will be staying this summer – but believes he can overcome the Chelsea boo-boys if he does not depart for Manchester City.

Fernandez received a mixed reaction in their final friendly at Stamford Bridge before the Premier League begins. The 25-year-old Argentinian replaced Reece James against Real Sociedad – and took the captain’s armband – as he was both jeered and cheered by his own fans.

Speaking on the eve of the 2026-27 season starting, and with Chelsea away at Fulham on Monday, Alonso said: 'It's not unusual. It can happen. We support him. We have a great player with Enzo, a top player, so important. I am happy that when I see him training, you see that he has a competitive mentality. We work with him every day very well.’

Alonso also hinted Fernandez would remain his vice-captain under James. Asked if he can see Chelsea’s supporters getting behind the midfielder, Alonso added: ‘I’m sure it will happen because this is a normal situation in football. Once we start the competition, we need the support.

‘We need the full commitment of all the team and of all the supporters when they come to Stamford Bridge. That we are pushing in the same direction.’

Xabi Alonso has refused to be drawn on whether Enzo Fernandez will be a Chelsea player when the transfer window closes

City's interest in Fernandez has been no secret this summer, though the side managed by Enzo Maresca have yet to submit a formal offer for the Argentina international. Chelsea were previously asking for £120million, but the Blues say those terms expired with the deadline they set for bids last Friday. City could be quoted a higher asking price if they sought one now.

Alonso dodged answering any and all questions about whether Fernandez would be staying with Chelsea at his pre-Fulham press conference, choosing instead to highlight how well he is training.

‘Enzo is a Chelsea player,’ Alonso said when asked directly if Fernandez would still be with Chelsea beyond deadline day. ‘He's a top, top player. He's training really well since he started 10 days ago with the team, very integrated. We are happy with him and he's getting ready for Monday.

‘He's training really well. I see him with a good attitude. That's what we want. He’s a player, he’s training well, he’s preparing for Monday and that’s my concern at the moment.’

Fernandez was previously used as a No 10 at Chelsea, though Alonso did hint he sees him in a deeper role rather than competing with Cole Palmer and Morgan Rogers.

‘He can do both,’ Alonso said. ‘I think when he's with the ball, he has the qualities to link the short passes but the long ones as well. He's able to see short and the farther players and from there he can progress. But he’s played great as a No 10 as well.’

Sports.title: No ego, refreshingly candid and the polar opposite of Oliver Glasner: This is what I learned from Pierre Sage's brilliant first press conference as Crystal Palace boss - from his tactical 'three pillars' to transfer clues on Sarr, Wharton and more
Sports.content:
No ego, refreshingly candid and the polar opposite of Oliver Glasner: This is what I learned from Pierre Sage's brilliant first press conference as Crystal Palace boss - from his tactical 'three pillars' to transfer clues on Sarr, Wharton and more

Unlock more from Bobby Manzi inside the Palace camp with a DailyMail+ subscription - brilliant exclusives, in-depth insight, analysis and more

Crystal Palace's press suite has benefitted from a luxurious summer refurbishment. Not only have the plastic chairs better suited to a school classroom been replaced by rows of leather seating, there is also a new man in the hotseat.

Palace have erased any lasting memories of Oliver Glasner – who switched allegiances to their new rivals Nottingham Forest – changing the layout of the room, the screens and brutally ripping the photo of the Austrian celebrating the club's FA Cup win off the wall.

In his place sat Pierre Sage, the French coach who secured Champions League football at Lens last season and won the French Cup. An intelligent, dignified and sincere communicator.

Sage sat with the media for 40 minutes on Thursday, and the main takeaway was this: he could not be more different to his predecessor.

There are just two striking similarities between Sage and Glasner – they play the same formation and are fascinated by social science. Sage, after all, lectured on sports mentality for 10 years at Claude Bernard University in Lyon.

Even in his first Premier League press conference, the differences between Crystal Palace's new boss Pierre Sage (pictured) and his predecessor Oliver Glasner were evident

Glasner's dealings with the media were often spiky last season, as he complained whenever he didn't get his way

At the start of the year, Glasner's interactions with the press were spiky. He frequently played mind games with the club and its supporters, throwing his toys out of the pram – rightly or wrongly – whenever he did not get his own way. It was box office but draining.

Sage, on the other hand, was refreshing. There was no equivocating, just candid conversation. Despite admitting he is a reserved character, he sat down and exuded a genuine transparency.

'I’m quiet, shy, maybe,' Sage said. 'But when I speak and I’m hungry, they know.'

Perhaps that is because he is not a product of the football establishment. There was no professional playing career, he had nothing handed to him. Sage was an amateur footballer and coach with an aspiration shared by millions: elite football.

'Four or five years ago, my dream was to become a member of staff – not a manager – at a pro team... I did it,' Sage added. 'But I did it in a way I didn’t consider and I became a head coach. It works well. That’s why I told myself I needed a new dream, and two years ago that dream became coming to the Premier League. Now I am here. I have to build another dream.

'I’m a flag bearer of the amateur coach and for young coaches to give them hope to become a head coach of a good team, a professional team. You need to work every day. To have an opportunity, you have to be an opportunity yourself.

'I came from the bottom. Now I’m here, I just want to give my best. I have no pressure. For me, the pressure is giving the players the best session I can give every day. Sometimes there will be a gap between what we did in game and what we chose before the game. But our job is to make the gap as small as we can, improve the way we play and develop our game.'

'Two years ago my dream became coming to the Premier League,' said Sage. 'Now I am here. I have to build another dream'

Sage accepted it may take a while to place his imprint on the team, with staggered arrivals throughout pre-season because 13 Palace players were at the World Cup. But he will adopt Glasner's style of play to an extent and gradually integrate his ideas to ensure Palace get off to the best start possible.

That was not laying the groundwork for an excuse, though, just pragmatism. He still expects results from himself and his team from week one, starting at Everton on Saturday.

'We have to consider the late arrivals of the players and accept what the players are able to do collectively now,' Sage added. 'But we want to implement our principles because that will give us more options to win games.

'We will do that session after session, game after game. The most important thing is to play as a team, respect every moment of play and every moment of the game because we want to play as a unit.

'I always speak about three pillars. The first is about pressing, we want to recover the ball as soon as we can because we want to play with the ball and be efficient in build-up, creating good possession conditions in the opponents' half. At the end, we want to attack the depths (high areas) and put pressure, psychological pressure and space pressure on the opponents in games.

'We are able to do that in transition and by having the ball in possession. We want to be able to play in a lot of contexts to compete. We have a focus on set-pieces because they’re important to win games and make a difference in some moments.'

Could transfer exits rock the boat?

As far as Sage is concerned, Adam Wharton, Ismaila Sarr and Daniel Munoz will all remain at Palace beyond the closure of the summer transfer window.

Manchester City enquired for Wharton but were knocked back, with Palace maintaining he is not for sale. In any case, their current valuation of the midfielder exceeds £100million.

Meanwhile, Galatasaray had a bid north of £30million turned down for Sarr this week. Palace value the Senegal international significantly above his market value.

Everton have assessed Munoz, although they are currently exploring moves for other targets at right back.

Besides Romain Esse, who Sage explicitly stated was not a part of his plans, the Palace boss is looking to build his squad, not dismantle it further. Daily Mail Sport understands Palace want to add two centre backs and a midfielder before the window closes.

Manchester City have shown interest in Palace midfielder Adam Wharton but the club are adamant he's not for sale

'We will, we will,' Sage responded when asked if Palace will keep Sarr. 'He’s a really important player for the club and for us. He played in the World Cup with Senegal and joined the group three weeks ago. He will be able to play this weekend.'

'We did it (sold players) and now it’s not the moment to do that,' he said of Wharton's future. 'He is able to play in another club, a big club, here or anywhere in Europe. But one year with us and a new dynamic will be good for him. We need him and that’s why he will stay with us. I hope he continues his improvement.'

As for Munoz, Sage was blunt: 'I hear the noise but he is happy to be with us and we are happy he is here.'

He applied the pressure on the recruitment team, too, urging them to sign a centre back with Premier League experience. Palace are in talks to loan Axel Disasi from Chelsea.

Palace will start the Premier League season without a central centre back after Maxence Lacroix joined Chelsea. They are also yet to secure a replacement for Marc Guehi, who left the club seven months ago.

Glasner would have used that as a stick to beat the board with. It became his transfer window trademark, lambasting the board for sluggish business.

Sage, instead, made his point – but with humility. Whether a level-headed approach will work with Palace chairman Steve Parish remains to be seen; Glasner's rants often sprang him into action.

Deep down, Sage will be annoyed he is starting the season with an incomplete backline but publicly he toed the party line and said he would rather wait for the right option. The sign of a leader without ego.

Does Matheus Franca have a future at Palace?

It has been a tough three years for Matheus Franca since arriving at Palace. He signed for £17million as a promising teenager from Brazil and took Wilfried Zaha's number 11 shirt.

The expectations were high for a player most knew nothing about and he subsequently faltered at every opportunity. He has played just 14 league games for Palace, spending most of the time injured or out of favour.

Last season, he went back to Brazil to join Vasco da Gama on loan. He did not set the world alight there either.

But there has been a glimpse of the player Palace had such high hopes for in pre-season, with Franca scoring four times and looking comfortable playing as a No9 rather than his usual position out wide.

Matheus Franca has had a difficult sime since moving to Palace from Brazil as a teenager, but his performances in pre-season have been encouraging

New manager Sage believes all is not lost on Franca: 'He had a good pre-season with four goals. It was difficult for him as he began here, that’s why he went on loan to Brazil last year.

'He has to adapt to European football because it’s really different to South American football. He’s shown really good things and we will see what we will do with him. We have to build the best context for him to improve because he’s young but he has talent.'

Where does Cheick Doucoure fit in?

Cheick Doucoure has not played a competitive game in 18 months after rupturing his ACL just a year after recovering from an achilles injury. The midfielder, once touted with a £70million move to Liverpool, has had multiple years shaved off his career.

Yet after a stable pre-season, he is back at Palace's disposal and ready to play in the Premier League. It will take time before he is anywhere near his best. There is a chance he will never be the same player he was. Nevertheless, Sage is excited to work with an 'incredible player'.

'He’s able to start,' said Sage. 'He didn’t play much during the last two seasons so we have to consider him within this situation. He needs time to come back and we will take our time to let him in a good context, particularly on the psychological side.

'When you play, you have to be confident, understand this moment is only a step and in a few moments you will be the player you were two years ago. That’s why we will take our time with him.

'He understands that. He walks a lot around the session but he’s really happy to be on the pitch and we are happy to see him on the pitch because he’s an incredible player.'

Sports.title: Juventus star faces missing start of the new football season after a FAN two-foot tackled and injured his hero in pitch invasion gone wrong
Sports.content:
Juventus defender Federico Gatti is at risk of missing the opening match of their Serie A season through injury after being bizarrely tackled by a fan during a pre-season match.

Gatti had been playing in an annual pre-match fixture at the Allianz Stadium, which sees Juventus' first team take on their NextGen side.

As part of the tradition of the match, fans typically invade the pitch during the latter stages of the event, which is billed as a family-friendly celebration.

The pitch invasion began early this year, with one fan jumping over the barriers and racing onto the field of play, with hundreds more following.

Footage showed the fan racing across the pitch in the direction of Gatti, who was facing away and unaware of the supporter.

An unfortunate slip saw the fan lose balance and slide two-footed into the Juventus defender at speed, knocking the Italian to the ground.

"Ausilio è un incapace perché non riesce a far fuori gli esuberi"



E per tanti (troppi) questa roba qua diventa "sogno bagnato" pic.twitter.com/tP1PRgklKx — Paolo (@Paolo78475202) August 18, 2026

Juventus defender Federico Gatti was slide tackled by a fan during a pre-season friendly

The fan, who participated in a traditional pitch invasion, slipped when approaching the unaware Gatti and sent the defender crashing to the pitch

Gatti was forced to miss Juventus' latest training session and is now reportedly a doubt for their opening match of the season this weekend

Other fans were quickly on the scene of the incident, which fortunately ended without Gatti suffering a serious injury.

The 28-year-old Italian, however, was still forced to miss Juventus' latest training session on Thursday with an ankle problem sustained from the fan's accidental slide tackle.

While Gatti sitting out of training was seen as a precaution, Gazzetta Dello Sport reported that there is a chance the defender could miss their opening Serie A match with Frosinone on Sunday.

Juventus are now said to be reconsidering the future format of the annual friendly following the incident.

Along with Gatti's issue, the club has reportedly determined that £43,000 of damage had also been caused at the Allianz Stadium at the event, which needs to be repaired ahead of their first home game of the season.

Sports.title: Liverpool expected to make improved offer for Brighton for winger Yankuba Minteh after £50m bid was rejected - with club still locked in talks with PSG in deal for Bradley Barcola
Sports.content:
Liverpool expected to make improved offer for Brighton for winger Yankuba Minteh after £50m bid was rejected - with club still locked in talks with PSG in deal for Bradley Barcola

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Liverpool are expected to make an improved offer for Brighton winger Yankuba Minteh after having a £50m bid rejected.

The Gambian is out until October after undergoing surgery on his right leg.

Liverpool reverted to the 22-year-old after considering Ibrahim Mbaye of Paris St Germain too expensive. They are continuing discussions for Bradley Barcola.

Daily Mail Sport reported upon Mohamed Salah’s departure that the Gambia international would feature on a list to bolster the wide forward position this summer.

While talks for Barcola are ongoing, they would preferably like two forwards with Ibrahim Mbaye, also of PSG, one sounded out last week.

Minteh is currently on the sidelines after suffering an injury in Brighton's pre-season win over Roma earlier this month.

Liverpool have approached Brighton over signing winger Yankuba Minteh this summer

Andoni Iraola's side are in the market to sign two forwards, with the club locked in talks over PSG's Bradley Barcola

Minteh has made 73 appearances for Brighton to date since joining from Newcastle in a £30m move in the summer of 2024. He has scored 10 goals and provided nine assists for the Seagulls.

Minteh predominantly plays on the right wing, but has also been used on the left by Fabian Hurzeler.

Meanwhile, Curtis Jones will have a medical at noon on Friday after Liverpool agreed to sell him to Inter Milan for £26.7m plus £4m in bonuses and a 10 percent sell-on.

The six-time England international, who joined Liverpool aged nine, has had his heart set on a move to Serie A for some time after failing to regularly establish himself as a starter at Anfield.

Liverpool are preparing for their first season under new manager Andoni Iraola, who replaced Arne Slot following the Dutchman's dismissal at the end of last season.

After spending over £450million on new signings including Alexander Isak, Florian Wirtz and Hugo Ekitike last summer, the 2024-25 Premier League champions struggled to reach the same heights again under the Dutchman and only narrowly managed to qualify for the Champions League with a fifth-place finish last term.

Liverpool, who waved farewell to Mohamed Salah, Andrew Robertson and Ibrahima Konate at the start of the summer, have so far recruited centre-half Jeremy Jacquet from Stade Rennais and left winger Victor Munoz from Osasuna ahead of the new campaign.

Sports.title: PREMIER LEAGUE PREDICTIONS: Our experts pick which side will win title, who will go down, biggest flop and best new signing ahead of the new season
Sports.content:
It's been a long 12 weeks since the final day of the 2025-26 season but football fans can finally rejoice - the Premier League is back.

With a bang, too. Liverpool, Manchester City, Chelsea, and Newcastle are just a clutch of the boldfaced names with new managers to keep an eye on, and anticipation is rising to see the summer rebuilds clubs have ushered in.

Now, on the eve of the return of top-flight football, Daily Mail Sport experts Oliver Holt, Ian Herbert, Mike Keegan, Kieran Gill, Lewis Steele and make their final predictions.

Tip to win the Premier League

Oliver Holt: Arsenal – they have made two good signings over the summer so far and sold prudently. They have strengthened from a position of strength. They look like a side that will be liberated by the confidence of being champions.

Ian Herbert: Arsenal - crossing the Rubicon to claim the title means so much, removes so much pressure. An excellent transfer window has made them stronger

Arsenal have got the devil off their back by wining their first Premier League title under Mikel Arteta and look stronger than ever

Chelsea welcome Xabi Alonso to Stamford Bridge unburdened by European football and having made key summer signings

Mike Keegan: Chelsea. We saw last season what an absence of European football can do at Manchester United and I like what I have seen at Stamford Bridge this summer given their recruitment pivot. The manager is top class and the old heads they have brought in could be enough for a stunning title assault.

Riath Al-Samarrai: Arsenal. They have the best squad, the least turbulence and have dismantled the mental barriers that previously dominated these conversations. The team to beat.

Kieran Gill: Arsenal. They are more settled than everyone else with Manchester City, Liverpool and Chelsea going through transitions under new managers. I’m not sure it will even be a close title race.

Lewis Steele: Arsenal. Best team by a distance last season. Manchester City were only close because the Gunners kept on stumbling and keeping them alive. Now, Mikel Arteta’s men will not have the tag of ‘bottlers’ or ‘chokers’ and that will free them up. I’d not be surprised if they won by 10 or more points.

Matt Barlow: Arsenal. Long time since they won back-to-back but strong and stable with main rivals in various degrees of flux. Bruno Guimaraes will improve them. Confident in the knowledge they have what it takes. Free from the anxiety of old.

Bobby Manzi: Arsenal appear stronger than last season, so this will no doubt be proved foolish come the end of the season. But Chelsea have an intelligent manager, have added experience to their squad and no European football to contend with - enabling them to focus on domestic glory. Alonso, against all odds, won the league invincible at Bayer Leverkusen. Chelsea look a good outside bet.

Completing the top four

Oliver Holt: Liverpool, Manchester City, Chelsea. For different reasons, Florian Wirtz and Alexander Isak had disappointing seasons with Liverpool last season. Both can flourish this year and Liverpool have new signings to complement them. Chelsea have a first class manager, no European commitments and a more realistic recruitment policy. City have the muscle-memory of previous greatness.

Ian Herbert: Chelsea, Tottenham, Manchester United. Something about Roberto de Zerbi’s energy allied to the big spending makes me think Spurs will be a big story this season. Chelsea on the up, too, but transition time for Manchester City and Liverpool

Mike Keegan: Arsenal will not be far off. You can’t judge City on a Community Shield but, for me, the jury remains firmly out on Enzo Maresca. Liverpool will improve under Andoni Iraola.

Alexander Isak endured a difficult first season at Liverpool but will be a major weapon fully fit

Riath Al-Samarrai: Liverpool, Manchester City, Chelsea. I don’t envision any of them making a sustained run on Arsenal, but a lot will depend on how quickly Liverpool adapt to Iraola’s style. That’s typically a slow process and a rapid finish. I can see them leading the chase.

Kieran Gill: Chelsea in second, City in third, Liverpool in fourth. Perhaps I’m thinking a tad optimistically on behalf of Xabi Alonso, but he is a good manager who has wielded his influence this summer.

Lewis Steele: Liverpool. People are sleeping on the ability of a much-improved Alexander Isak and Florian Wirtz. Their XI is very good but beyond that, it is a worry. Manchester City because they have a deep squad and did not deserve the overreaction or ridicule that came after losing a glorified friendly but losing Pep Guardiola, Bernardo Silva, Rodri and John Stones in the same summer rips their heart out. I’ll go with Chelsea in fourth as I like Xabi Alonso.

Matt Barlow: Chelsea, Liverpool, and Man City. I'm expecting Xabi Alonso to get a tune out of the mass of talent at Chelsea, Liverpool’s big signings from 2025 to improve and City to fade post-Pep Guardiola and post-Rodri but still have lots of quality and Erling Haaland’s goals.

Bobby Manzi: Arsenal, Man United, Man City. Arsenal are nailed on for the top two but will find the first couple of weeks without William Saliba difficult. Manchester United have executed intelligent summer business - they had to improve their midfield and they have. Youri Tielemans, Andrey Santos and Carlos Baleba are a great blend. As long as Michael Carrick was not a one-hit wonder, they will be up there. A new era at Manchester City but they still have a strong squad to creep into the top four.

The three going down

Oliver Holt: Newcastle almost got sucked into a relegation battle last season. Since then, they’ve lost their biggest asset, Eddie Howe, and their three best players, Anthony Gordon, Bruno Guimaraes and Sandro Tonali. Their Saudi owners appear to have disconnected. I like Gary O’Neil, the Ipswich boss, but Ipswich are a classic yo-yo club. And I don’t think Hull have enough to stay up.

Ian Herbert: Fulham, Coventry and Ipswich. Fulham seem a perfect storm: inexperienced new manager, good players have left, an attempt to introduce new system to a club lacking intensity last season. There’s a bond about Hull City. I suspect they’ll be OK.

Newcastle have seen their ranks depleted and a successful manager depart ahead of the start of the season

Mike Keegan: Sunderland, Ipswich Town, Hull City. I’ll probably be the only one predicting Sunderland and I wish I wasn’t because they’re a great club with great fans but they massively overachieved last season and European football this time around could be a killer.

Riath Al-Samarrai: Hull, Ipswich, Fulham. That’s putting a certain amount of faith in Coventry, but Fulham have lost a strong manager and their best player in Harry Wilson. I think they’ll struggle.

Kieran Gill: Ipswich, Hull, Sunderland. I have a hunch that Coventry under Frank Lampard will surprise us, while Sunderland may struggle juggling European football with everything else.

Lewis Steele: Going to be boring and say the three promoted teams. I do think Sunderland will struggle from a bit of second-season syndrome but I think they have just enough quality with Enzo Le Fee, Granit Xhaka, Brian Brobbey et al.

Matt Barlow: Ipswich, Hull, Coventry. Those coming up can all take inspiration from last season’s survivors and there some established teams should be worried by the radical summer of change including Newcastle, Fulham and Palace but the gap still yawns.

Bobby Manzi: Coventry, Hull, Ipswich. Quite simply, the promoted sides are not better than any of the other 17 sides. Coventry have the best chance of staying up but they are lacking in defence.

The biggest overachievers will be

Oliver Holt: Spurs – they have bought well in the summer and in Roberto de Zerbi, they have one of the best managers of this generation. Like Chelsea, they have no European football to drain their resources. They’ll put their recent struggles behind them in style although they could do with a new striker.

Ian Herbert: Everton - drab end to last season obscured the way that David Moyes, such a fine and still underrated manager, has rescued them from annual purgatory. Some good recruits this summer. Moyes buys well. Europe calls.

Mike Keegan: Chelsea, followed by Coventry, who I think will defy the odds and stay up.

Riath Al-Samarrai: Brentford. Again. A smart club with a smart plan and they haven’t been raided quite like Brighton, who would be my second choice if they didn’t have to content with European commitments.

Kieran Gill: I may have hinted at this in my previous answer, but I’ll plump for Coventry. I’m not saying they will suddenly secure Europe. That’s a stretch. Somewhere towards the midtable would be cool.

Lewis Steele: A Brighton or Bournemouth could really flourish but may be held back by Europe. After finishing 17th twice in a row, lowly relegation fodder Spurs might climb up the table…

Tottenham have recruited intensely over the summer, luring Sandro Tonali from Newcastle in a bid to avoid a third 17th-place finish in three seasons

Matt Barlow: Leeds - finished last season at a gallop and reinforced in the summer market. Three winnable home fixtures to start at fortress Elland Road can build a platform for a strong season as others from mid table tackle complications of Europe

Bobby Manzi: Brentford. They were so close to Europe last season - missing out on goal difference. Many tipped them to go down under Keith Andrews and they defied expectation. This season, they may just get Europe. With Bournemouth, Crystal Palace, Sunderland and Brighton all playing on Thursday nights, the teams in the middle of the pack could suffer a drop-off in the league. Brentford have kept the majority of their squad from last season together and added sprinkles of quality such as Mamadou Sangare in midfield. They appear well positioned.

The biggest underachievers will be…

Oliver Holt: Manchester City – I know I’ve got City down to finish in my top four but I don’t think they’ll challenge for the title. It’s always tough when a great manager leaves a club after a long time in charge and I don’t think it will be any different for City. It’s a huge test for Enzo Maresca.

Ian Herbert: Newcastle – car crash summer from a club the Saudis couldn’t be bothered to administer properly, now led by a managerial novice. You’re well out of it, Eddie.

Mike Keegan: Manchester United. There is time left in the transfer window for United to strengthen but, as things stand, I do not think they have made the additions which will deliver another Champions League finish.

Riath Al-Samarrai: A three-way tie between Manchester United (thin squad), Newcastle (decimated squad and technical area) and Aston Villa (great expectations after last season but a pretty horrible summer of departures).

Kieran Gill: Aston Villa. As good of a manager as Unai Emery is, Villa have sold some big names this summer, from Morgan Rogers to Lucas Digne to Youri Tielemens, so I’m concerned they may struggle.

Aston Villa have seen their squad stripped of a number of key talents and have European tests to come later in the season

Lewis Steele: Newcastle. The bubble has burst. I did think it was probably right for Eddie Howe to move on but losing Sandro Tonali, Bruno Guimaraes and Anthony Gordon in the same window stinks.

Matt Barlow: Aston Villa. Challenging season ahead for Unai Emery. Lost Morgan Rogers, Youri Tielemans and Lucas Digne. Ezri Konsa leaving. Emi Martinez and Ollie Watkins unsettled. Key staff gone, too. And has a Champions League campaign to plot.

Bobby Manzi: Bourmemouth. It’s only natural to have a comedown after last season, finishing sixth on 57 points and securing Europa League football for the first time. Much like with Palace last season, playing Thursday-Sunday will take its toll domestically. A bottom-half finish but a strong European return for the Cherries.

Player of the season

Oliver Holt: There are early signs that Arsenal may have cast off the nerves that afflicted them last season. If they play with more freedom and justify their tag as favourites, Bukayo Saka may rediscover his best form.

Ian Herbert: Declan Rice was the orchestrator and architect of so much about Arsenal last season. I can see him running a side that’s feeling mentally released and free.

Mike Keegan: Cole Palmer. A summer off is incredibly rare in this world of saturated football and the mysteriously-omitted England winger will have a barnstormer.

Riath Al-Samarrai: Easy answer would be Haaland, again, but I’ll go with Odegaard at Arsenal. He looks fit and sharp again, which wasn’t always the case last season, but it’ll be interesting to see how Arteta constructs the puzzle with Rice and Guimaraes (who might well be the star turn – the guy can do everything).

Cole Palmer has had a summer off after an injury-stricken season and should be raring to go

Kieran Gill: Joao Pedro. Just because of what I’ve seen of him in Chelsea’s handful of pre-season games. He’s looking like a superstar, and it is understood he is set to sign a new contract.

Lewis Steele: Since I cover Liverpool I will keep my regular readers happy by going with Isak. I’ll look silly when he does his hamstring on Sunday.

Matt Barlow: Alexander Isak. Back to full fitness after his awful first season at Liverpool and sure to enjoy Andoni Iraola’s full throttle style.

Bobby Manzi: Erling Haaland. Goals, goals, goals. At the World Cup, Haaland proved he can find the back of the net regardless of who is around him - scoring seven in five matches. He’s a machine. Nobody will get close to him.

Signing of the summer (so far)

Oliver Holt: Jordan Henderson – not just because he still retains much of the quality he had in his prime but because he is a symbol of a change in approach that Chelsea desperately needed. Xabi Alonso has some brilliant young players at his disposal but it has to be leavened with experience and Henderson and Danny Welbeck are fine professionals who will provide that.

Ian Herbert: Bruno Guimaraes will look even classier in a world class midfield and his presence will free up Rice. Some tandem they’ll be. The £75m salary may come to look excellent value.

Mike Keegan: Youri Tielemans. For the first time in a long time, Manchester United have signed a player who looks like a Manchester United player. I think he’ll settle quickly at Old Trafford and a much-needed all-round presence in midfield.

Riath Al-Samarrai: Harry Wilson to Leeds for nothing.

Kieran Gill: Arsenal’s £75m landing of Bruno Guimaraes from Newcastle. He should fit into that midfield beside Declan Rice and Martin Odegaard nicely.

Bruno Guimaraes represents a coup for Arsenal's recruitment after his move from Newcastle

Lewis Steele: I like some of the low-key ones like Joao Gomes to Aston Villa and Ousmane Diomande to Nottingham Forest and Antonio Silva to Bournemouth. But for the sake of picking one I’ll go Matheus Fernandes.

Matt Barlow: Maxence Lacroix. Should bring much needed leadership and maturity to the heart of Chelsea’s young team and not bad value in today’s world of head-spinning fees.

Bobby Manzi: Youri Tielemans. Manchester United have been gradually improving their squad to mount a title charge by 2028. Last season they bought a new forward line; this season it is the midfield. £35million for one of the best midfielders in the league who is in his peak is the best pound-for-pound signing of a window where midfielders are moving for £100m-plus. Technical Tielemans will give United control of games from deep alongside contributing goals and assists.

The signing I'm not sure about is…

Oliver Holt: It hasn’t happened yet but if it does, I think Enzo Fernandez to Manchester City would be a mistake that would upset the balance and the ethos of the club.

Ian Herbert: Andrey Santos. A curious and very substantial £50m layout on a player who doesn’t really seem to have proved himself as a stellar talent at Chelsea. Odd summer for United.

Mike Keegan: James Trafford. I like Trafford. He’s down-to-earth, a character and clearly a talented shot-stopper. However, in this era of set-piece coaches and goals from corners, I do wonder if he has the physical presence to ensure he lives up to his £40m fee.

Riath Al-Samarrai: Sandro Tonali at Tottenham. The price tag is astronomical.

Kieran Gill: Alejandro Garnacho. Aston Villa have taken a chance on him with a loan – and a conditional obligation to buy – and he has a ton to prove.

Alejandro Garnacho remains a risky deal for Aston Villa after his uneven season in west London

Lewis Steele: Carlos Baleba to Manchester United if it happens. Brighton fans don’t seem bothered about him leaving.

Matt Barlow: Elliot Anderson. Quality player but a huge fee brings great expectation and a difficult time to join Manchester City at the end of an era.

Bobby Manzi: Luka Vuskovic. A teenage defender with a very high ceiling but £50m is a significant outlay for a centre-back who hasn’t played in the Premier League and still has plenty of development ahead of him. He will make mistakes this season - he’s young. Brighton just have to hope he fulfils his potential and eventually reaches his projected future sell-on value. After all, their model is based on calculated risks.

Manager with the most to prove

Oliver Holt: It has to be Enzo Maresca. Following Pep Guardiola is the toughest task in world football and that is Maresca’s fate. Far from universally popular at Leicester City, he left Chelsea in difficult circumstances. I’m not sure he has the personality or the people skills to lead a club of City’s size. If he does, he will join the elite of world coaching.

Ian Herbert: Enzo Maresca. The expectation will be that the prophet of Pep will simply pick up his reins, but history, his own temperament and the Community Shield tell us otherwise. Spectre of those 115 Premier League charges still a shadow on the wall.

Mike Keegan: Xabi Alonso. He got the big gig and, to say it didn’t go well, would appear to be a significant understatement. Arrives at Stamford Bridge with a big point to prove post-Real Madrid, and I think he will do just that.

Enzo Maresca is stepping into enormous shoes at the Etihad as he replaces his former boss Pep Guardiola at Man City

Riath Al-Samarrai: Enzo Maresca at Manchester City, obviously. Seemed a little too pleased with some half-decent work at Chelsea and those shoes he is filling at City are huge.

Kieran Gill: Enzo Maresca. Following Pep Guardiola is no easy task, but Manchester City paid Chelsea a total of £17m to hire him. That brings immediate pressure at a club used to winning.

Lewis Steele: Enzo Maresca. Everyone is out to get him as we saw with the vultures descending on a glorified friendly defeat against the best team in the country. He has a lot of doubters to silence. Same goes for Andoni Iraola, Xabi Alonso, the list goes on…

Matt Barlow: Enzo Maresca. Just the 15 major trophies in 10 years for Pep Guardiola, follow that.

Bobby Manzi: Alvaro Arbeloa. Arbeloa is a bit of an unknown quantity. Interim at Real Madrid for five months at the end of last season, having previously held youth roles, this is his first genuine crack at senior management. His record at Real was okay with a 64.29 per cent win rate, losing eight games. That would be more than acceptable at Fulham, not so much at Real. But he was credited for how he lifted the dressing room after a tough spell under Alonso. Fulham have enjoyed stability in recent years under Marco Silva: Arbeloa must show he can provide that.

Sports.title: Man United progressing in Carlos Baleba talks with Brighton, Aston Villa table Ollie Watkins contract offer amid Saudi interest, and Man City see Adam Wharton enquiry rebuffed: WINDOW WATCH
Sports.content:
Man United progressing in Carlos Baleba talks with Brighton, Aston Villa table Ollie Watkins contract offer amid Saudi interest, and Man City see Adam Wharton enquiry rebuffed: WINDOW WATCH

It's that time of the year again – the transfer window is now open until September 1 and it's sure to be a busy period as clubs look to make big signings ahead of the new season.

Here are today's latest developments from Simon Jones and the Daily Mail Sport team...

Man United progressing in Baleba talks

Manchester United are continuing discussions over a fee with Brighton for Carlos Baleba.

Brighton have rejected United’s £60million plus £5m for the midfielder but talks have been progressing to a compromise.

The 22-year-old Cameroon international is hoping the deal can be wrapped up over the weekend.

Meanwhile, United right-back Habeeb Ogunneye is scheduled to undergo a medical with Arsenal ahead of his move there.

The deal is understood to be a free transfer with 40percent sell-on clause.

The 20-year-old is being signed to boost numbers with Arsenal’s U21s but also train with the first team.

Man United have had a £65m offer for Carlos Baleba rejected but talks are progressing with Brighton

Clubs circle for Jackson

Atletico Madrid have enquired about a loan deal for Chelsea striker Nicolas Jackson.

Atletico director Mateu Alemany was understood to have travelled to London on Thursday for talks.

Jackson also has interest from Aston Villa, Napoli and Saudi Arabia.

Spurs talk numbers

Tottenham are working on figures with City for Savinho and forward Omar Marmoush. The deal for Savinho could be worth up to £84m.

City have also asked about Crystal Palace midfielder Adam Wharton as they work through a list of targets.

Leeds swoop for goalkeeper Zetterer

Leeds United are closing on a deal for Eintracht Frankfurt goalkeeper Michael Zetterer to come in as James Trafford's deputy.

The clubs are finalising agreement for the 31-year-old, but Frankfurt need to find a new goalkeeper to replace Zetterer first.

Leeds are waiting for Lucas Perri to fully recover from a minor injury before he completes his delayed loan move to Torino.

Zetterer, 31, is a former Germany U21 international.

Southampton reject Villa approach for Harwood-Bellis

Aston Villa have been rebuffed in an enquiry for Southampton defender Taylor Harwood-Bellis.

Villa are willing to offer around £17.5m for the 24-year-old but Saints had already rejected a similar offer from Benfica.

Talks are ongoing as Villa assess options such as Tosin Adarabioyo at Chelsea and Fikayo Tomori of AC Milan to fill the void left by Ezri Konsa's move to Arsenal.

Villa have been rebuffed in an enquiry for Southampton defender Taylor Harwood-Bellis

City keep watching brief on Wharton

Manchester City maintain an interest in Crystal Palace midfielder Adam Wharton.

The Selhurst Park club are reluctant to lose the 22-year-old this summer but have been making significant enquiries for midfielders in recent weeks.

City are exploring several options including Manu Kone at Roma while they are advancing in talks to sign Ayyoub Bouaddi from Lille and are assessing the cost of a bid for Chelsea's Enzo Fernandez.

'We did it [sold big players in the past], and now is not the moment to do that,' said Palace boss Pierre Sage on Thursday.

'He is able to play in another club, a big club. Here, or anywhere in Europe, but one year with us, in a new dynamic, will be good for him. And we need him - that is why I think he will stay with us.'

Wharton has been a significant Premier League performer in recent seasons and excelled in the Europa League Conference final but analysts at some top level would-be suitors have indicated his running statistics do not reflect someone who can fit into a high-pressing style.

He continues to show on the pitch, however, an ability to find the right pass and shield his defence.

City have also made contact with Palmeiras for winger Allan Elias as they seek a replacement for Savinho.

Allan, 22, wants to join City but his club are reluctant to sell now with their season running to December. Talks are ongoing over a £35million fee.

SIMON JONES AND BOBBY MANZI

Manchester City have seen an enquiry for Adam Wharton rebuffed by Crystal Palace

Jones set for Inter medical

Inter Milan expect Curtis Jones to arrive later today ahead of a £30.7million move from Liverpool. The Italian side have scheduled Jones' medical for midday on Friday.

Inter bid £26.7m plus £4m in add-ons with a 10 per cent sell-on clause, offering a similar structure to the deal used to sign Djed Spence from Tottenham.

Curtis Jones is set to sign a five-year deal with Inter

Jones, 25, will sign a five-year deal with the Serie A champions.

Meanwhile, Liverpool centre back Ifeanyi Ndukwe, 18, is in talks to join Levante on loan. Ndukwe does not qualify for a work permit in England so must be loaned out. Liverpool remain in talks over PSG winger Bradley Barcola.

Sheffield Wednesday are to confirm the signing of Liverpool's Northern Ireland international winger Kieran Morrison on a season-long loan.

Hammers close on Mukasa

West Ham are close to an agreement to sign highly-rated Manchester City forward Divine Mukasa on loan for the season.

There is no buy option for the 18-year-old who spent the second half of last season on loan at Leicester City

City step up hunt for Savinho replacement

Manchester City have asked about Palmeiras winger Allan Elias as they consider replacements for Savinho.

Allan is 22 but has not been capped by Brazil. Quick and skilful, he is not a goalscorer but has earned a reputation as a worker, willing to press.

Newcastle United and Aston Villa have also scouted him in recent months.

City are evaluating several options with Tottenham working on the deal to sign Savinho and forward Omar Marmoush.

Bayern reach Palhinha agreement

Bayern Munich have reached a full agreement with Benfica over the £17million sale of Joao Palhinha.

The 31-year-old midfielder had been a target for Aston Villa and Newcastle United but will now reunite with his former Fulham boss Marco Silva at Benfica.

Villa were only willing to take him on an initial loan which Bayern refused.

Villa table new contract offer to Watkins

Aston Villa have made a new contract offer to striker Ollie Watkins.

The 30-year-old is open to a move to Al Hilal who had a £38.5m offer rejected on Tuesday but are preparing a fourth offer for the England international.

Watkins has scored consistently throughout his Villa career and his goals would be difficult to replace.

Villa have maintained contacts over Chelsea's Nicolas Jackson who also has interest from Napoli but he is valued around £65m.

Aston Villa have put forward a new contract offer to striker Ollie Watkins

Wrexham make move for ex-United star

Wrexham are continuing discussions with free agent Axel Tuanzebe.

The 28-year-old Congo international left Burnley at the end of last season and has had interest from clubs but is interested in Wrexham's ambitious project.

Wrexham are in talks to sign former Manchester United defender Axel Tuanzebe

Palace return for Auxerre target

Crystal Palace have rekindled interest in Auxerre midfielder Kevin Danois.

The 22-year-old was discussed as an option in January and Palace have made further enquiries.

The France U21 international is an attacking player who can also play out wide and was on Newcastle United's list earlier in the year.

Hull advance in talks for Betis star Garcia

Hull City owner Acun Ilicali has confirmed they are making progress on their bid to sign Real Betis winger Pablo Garcia and remain in talks for Deportivo La Coruna winger Yeremay Hernandez.

'I think probably, if nothing unknown happens, we will see him in a black and gold shirt. It has to be finalised, but I would say 90 percent of this deal is done. We are talking about the last details,' said Ilicali.

Pictures of Hernandez in Hull have been posted on social media, and Ilicali told BBC Humberside: 'We have to get the club side done and Yeremay also wants to come but it is a very vital, critical decision for himself. This deal is a very hard deal but we are somewhere where it looks positive.

'He is a young boy and it would change his life completely so he wanted to see where he would come. We will see in three, four days if this deal will be done or not. If it happens it will be a record for sure.'

Race on for Black Cats Ta Bi

West Ham and Burnley have expressed interest in Sunderland winger Jocelin Ta Bi.

The 21-year-old only joined Sunderland from Maccabi Netanya in January and signed a four and a half year contract.

He made one appearance in the FA Cup against Oxford United and then started against Fulham in the Premier League.

As it stands, the Championship clubs have expressed interest but talks have not gone further.

Sports.title: Brother of Finlay Tarling will ride in Vuelta a Espana just eight days after British 19-year-old was fatally struck by van during race - and parents back him with brave statement
Sports.content:
Josh Tarling will start the Vuelta a Espana this weekend just eight days after the tragic death of his brother Finlay, his team have confirmed.

Tarling has been named in Netcompany INEOS's eight-man squad for the stage race, the third and final grand tour of the season, which begins on Saturday in Monaco.

The 22-year-old will take to the start line just eight days after his younger brother Finlay, 19, died during the Tour of Portugal.

The Welsh rider died last Friday after being struck by a van during the eighth stage of the race.

Police explained earlier this week that spectators had waved the van onto the road, having thought that all the cyclists in the race had gone past.

Netcompany INEOS were the last of the 23 teams to confirm their line-up for the Vuelta a Espana, having waited for Tarling's decision on whether he wanted to participate in the three-week race following the tragedy.

Josh Tarling will start the Vuelta a Espana this weekend, just eight days after the tragic death of his brother Finlay

Finlay, 19, tragically died last Friday following a crash during the Tour of Portugal

'La Vuelta is a big opportunity for us to finish the Grand Tour season strongly.

'I'm confident in the team we're taking and their ability to adapt to whatever the race throws at us over the next three weeks. It'll be a tough race, because La Vuelta always is, but the team is united and looking forward to taking it on.

'It also goes without saying that, as a team, we all fully support Josh in his decision to take part in the race.'

Josh's decision to race has been supported by parents Michael and Dawn, who stated their son chose to race in honour of his brother.

'On Saturday Joshua will be riding the Vuelta,' Michael and Dawn wrote on Instagram.

'He has chosen to do so in honour of his brother Fin, with the full support of his family, surrounded by a team who have been incredibly supportive of whatever decision he made.

'I could not have wished for two boys who were closer growing up and into adulthood we have watched with pride as Joshua has been the most loving and supportive big brother to Fin. Following this devastating news he has been an incredible strength for us all.

'Finlay was so incredibly proud of his big brother, and would be watching nose to the tv and shouting as he competed.

Parents Dawn and Michael, pictured with Finlay, have supported Josh's decision to race

'So it is right that Josh honours that love and pride by doing what Fin always loved watching him do.'

The post was accompanied with the hashtag 'ForFin'.

A GoFundMe page, authorised by Dawn and Michael, has been set up in memory of Finlay with the aim of funding future generations of young Welsh riders.

Over £70,000 has been donated to date.

Sports.title: Atletico Madrid 'agree to sell Julian Alvarez to Arsenal' - but there's a catch
Sports.content:
Atletico Madrid 'agree to sell Julian Alvarez to Arsenal' - but there's a catch

Julian Alvarez issued a public transfer request at the World Cup and Atletico Madrid appear to have finally accepted that selling him is now the only viable solution

View 2 Images Julian Alvarez wants to leave Atletico Madrid (Image: Juan Manuel Serrano Arce/Getty Images)

Atletico Madrid have finally changed their stance and are now open to selling Julian Alvarez to Arsenal - but the player remains steadfast in his desire to join Barcelona instead.

‌



Alvarez, 26, is desperate to join Barca, who saw their €100million (£86m) bid rejected earlier this summer and were the subject of a complaint to FIFA from Atletico for allegedly tapping the player up.

‌



That was the after Alvarez went public with his desire to leave during the World Cup. Atletico boss Diego Simeone declared earlier this month that the Argentina international's future had been decided, with the striker set to remain in Madrid for another season.

‌



But Spanish outlet Mundo Deportivo report that the situation has become untenable, forcing Atletico to accept a sale - except not to Barcelona. Simeone would even accept taking Arsenal's Viktor Gyokeres as part of a swap deal which has been mooted in recent weeks.

Alvarez, however, doesn't want to return to England, having chosen to leave Manchester City in 2024. His heart is set on joining Barcelona, which is believed to be his 'dream' club.

FOLLOW OUR ARSENAL FB PAGE! Latest Gunners news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

‌



Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

In June, Alvarez declared: "I spoke with people at the club, with those I had to speak with and the best thing for everyone is ‌a transfer and I want to fulfil my dream. It's not the time to talk about this, but I also can't hide ⁠it. I try to ⁠be an honest person."

CEO Miguel Angel Gil Marin has been firm, though, claiming that the only way in which Alvarez can be sold is if a club pays his extravagant €500million (£428m) release clause. "We don't want to transfer him," Gil Marin stated.

‌



"We didn't accept the €100m offer, nor will we accept one for €150m or €200m. I have no doubt that Atletico is the right place for Julian and that Julian is the centre forward for Atletico Madrid. We want to keep him."

Should Julian Alvarez join Arsenal? Have your say in the comments section.

View 2 Images Julian Alvarez didn't play in Atletico Madrid's opener (Image: Dennis Agyeman/Europa Press via Getty Images)

‌



Alvarez missed Atletico's first game of the La Liga season, a 2-0 win at home to Malaga. Simeone explained pre-match that the former City star wasn't match fit, having been granted extra time off after helping Argentina reach the World Cup final.

"We don't believe Julian Alvarez is in the right condition to play or take part for tomorrow's game," the Atletico boss said. "Hopefully, over these next four days, he'll make further progress and we'll be closer to where we want him to be.

"We're looking after both the person and the player, and we understand that he is not in the right condition to play in this match."

Article continues below

Atletico's next game is on Sunday, hosting Villarreal. It remains to be seen whether Alvarez will feature.

Sports.title: Anthony Joshua sets out demands to move Tyson Fury fight to New York
Sports.content:
Anthony Joshua sets out demands to move Tyson Fury fight to New York

Joshua has insisted he wants the all-British heavyweight showdown to take place at Wembley, but Netflix and the Saudi Arabian moneymen behind the fight want to stage it in the Big Apple

View Image Anthony Joshua has made his demands

Anthony Joshua has submitted his demands to move his fight with Tyson Fury to New York.

‌



Joshua has insisted he wants the all-British heavyweight showdown to take place at Wembley. But Netflix and the Saudi Arabian moneymen behind the fight want to stage it in the Big Apple. It is understood Joshua is willing to face Fury at Madison Square Garden on November 20 if he is compensated financially.

‌



The former two-time world champion will face a hike in his tax bill if the bout is moved across the Atlantic and wants his purse increased to reflect that. Joshua is also understood to be owed money from his come-from-behind knockout win over Kristrian Prenga last month. Additionally, promoter Eddie Hearn has sought assurances over ticketing and security for the event, as reported by Boxing Scene.

‌



Joshua and Fury signed separate contracts for the fight earlier this year but only Joshua's deal included a demand over the venue. He believes hosting the biggest fight in British boxing history in America will damage his legacy. But he is now ready to relent in order to bring an end to his decade-long feud with rival Fury. If Joshua's demands are met, an official announcement could follow next week.

Tyson Fury drops biggest Anthony Joshua fight hint yet after ultimatum READ MORE :

Joshua's demands come after Fury's manager Spencer Brown expressed his concern over the delay in announcing the fight. "Everybody's got a bit of doubt in their mind," he said in an interview with Sky Sports. "There's reasons you could think that. If you'd asked me a week ago, I'd have said no, but now it's a little bit concerning that things haven't progressed down the line. We need to get this fight on."

Article continues below

"You can't keep flogging a dead horse, can you? We've been flogging a dead horse for months now. We've waited and waited to do it at Wembley. The hope is fading that it's going to be at Wembley.

"A decision must be made. Let's get the fight on wherever it is, whether it's in Timbuktu or whether it's in Wembley Stadium. We just want to get it announced. People are getting bored. We're in danger of really boring people."

Sports.title: York Ebor Festival tips: Friday's best bets for EVERY race from our top tipster Newsboy
Sports.content:
1.50 Sky Bet Mile Handicap - EXCLUSIVE CODE has one big prize from a marquee summer meeting on his CV - and another may not be far away.

After fourth placings in a novice stakes at Newbury and a maiden at Goodwood - the latter on terrain with give in it - last summer, the three-year-old son of Blue Point returned from a 259-day abeyance to land a 25-runner maiden at the former track in April.

Archie Watson was then tempted to take aim at the Britannia Handicap over the straight mile at Royal Ascot, but a draw in stall three meant Exclusive Code’s challenge was over before it began.

Andrew Balding writes new ending to £1.5m summer blockbuster with unbeaten Item READ MORE :

In the circumstances, a 13th behind Moonfall - he came home third of the 15 horses racing towards the far side - was a decent effort and Exclusive Code went off a well-backed 2-1 favourite for the one-mile handicap for three-year-olds at Glorious Goodwood.

‌



James Doyle’s mount duly netted the money with a one-length beating of Zennor Storm and, with more to come, is the choice to stay ahead of the runner-up despite being on 4lb worse terms for the rematch.

Bearish , the progressive winner of his handicap debut at Ayr last time, is expected to go well, while Le Samourai and St Anton also make appeal.

NEWSBOY’S 1-2-3: 1 EXCLUSIVE CODE, 2 BEARISH, 3 ZENNOR STORM

View 7 Images Amiloc has been tipped by Newsboy

‌



2.25 Weatherbys Lonsdale Cup - AMILOC, at the centre of a calamity at Glorious Goodwood, should enjoy better luck today.

Unbeaten as a two-year-old in 2024, Postponed’s son continued his upward curve in the care of Ralph Beckett last season, coming home in front on the South Downs on his first two starts before tackling Group 2 company to land the King Edward VII Stakes at Royal Ascot.

Amiloc then moved up to the highest level and looked anything out of place in returning a four-length second to Al Riffa in the Irish St Leger over a mile and three-quarters at the Curragh and a staying-on fourth in the Breeders’ Cup Turf over two furlongs shorter at Del Mar.

My selection flopped when a well-backed 8-13 hotpot for the Group 2 Yorkshire Cup on the Knavesmire in May but his sixth to Giavellotto in the same-level Hardwicke Stakes back at Royal Ascot was much more like it.

‌



Amiloc attracted support for the Group 1 Goodwood Cup, his first attempt at two miles, 24 days ago but lurched to his left leaving the stalls and unshipped Hector Crouch, who makes way for Rossa Ryan here.

He therefore has to prove his staying power but shapes as if he will last the distance, and a bold show is on the cards. Caballo De Mar is feared most, ahead of Carmers and Mount Atlas.

NEWSBOY’S 1-2-3: 1 AMILOC, 2 CABALLO DE MAR, 3 MOUNT ATLAS

View 7 Images Michael Dods: trains Arapaho Gold (Image: PA)

‌



3.00 Al Basti Equiworld Dubai Gimcrack Stakes - ARAPAHO GOLD is unbeaten - and fancied to stay that way.

Michael Dods’ illustrious training career has seen the Co Durham trainer lift numerous big prizes, including Group 1 victories with Mecca’s Angel and Mabs Cross. And Arapaho Gold could be bound for the top level, based on the evidence of his three outings so far.

There was clearly some confidence behind the son of Bayside Boy when he began his career in a five-furlong maiden at Thirsk at the beginning of May - Arapaho Gold went off at 7-2 in a field of eight and won easily, beating Kodiak Breeze by two and a half lengths.

An evident mistrust of the starting stalls needs monitoring - my selection was withdrawn from at Beverley four weeks later after rearing up in the structure - but all was well when Connor Beasley’s partner returned to Thirsk to justify odds of 2-9 over six furlongs in July.

‌



His three-and-three-quarter-length humbling of Mick’s The Boy led to a challenge for the Listed Rose Bowl Stakes at Newbury a further 16 days on and, despite being barged into by an opponent early on, Arapaho Gold kept his composure to make it 3-3, leading at the furlong marker to hold Nabati by a neck.

There is plenty more where that came from, with Adaay In Scarlett, and Marco Polo and Mussab the best candidates for the podium.

NEWSBOY’S 1-2-3: 1 ARAPAHO GOLD, 2 ADAAY IN SCARLETT, 3 MARCO POLO

View 7 Images American Affair: Newsboy's pick

‌



3.35 Coolmore City Of Troy Nunthorpe Stakes - AMERICAN AFFAIR, back at the peak of his powers, earns the vote to double his Group 1 tally.

The Jim Goldie-trained speedster, having landed Doncaster’s Portland Handicap in September of the previous year, enjoyed an annus mirabilis in 2025.

American Affair started the campaign by beating Jm Jungle for the Scottish Sprint Cup Handicap at Musselburgh in April, had the same rival in second in a similar event over this afternoon’s course and distance the following month and then notched a first top-level triumph for both himself and his trainer with a neck call from Frost At Dawn in Royal Ascot’s King Charles III Stakes.

Plans to take in the Nunthorpe and the Breeders’ Cup were shelved when Washington DC’s son suffered a bone injury in a fetlock joint, and the road back in 2026 included defeats on his first four outings.

‌



But his connections’ patience received its reward as the six-year-old roared back to winning form in the Group 2 King George Stakes at Glorious Goodwood.

Leading at the halfway point of the five furlongs, American Affair charged home to beat Rumstar by half a length, with Time For Sandals (third), Asfoora (fourth), Jm Jungle (fifth), Partisan Hero (seventh), Night Raider (10th) and Azure Angel (15th) further back. There should be yet more to come and, proven on the track and on rain-softened terrain, American Affair ticks a lot of boxes.

Market leaders Rayevka and Bacio have something to recommend them, with two-year-old Pershaada and the improving Redorange others to throw into the mix.

View 7 Images Jane Chapple-Hyam trains Newsboy's tip (Image: Racing Photos via Getty Images)

‌



4.10 Assured Data Protection Handicap - PRIMO LARA has rediscovered his mojo - but remains well handicapped on his old form.

The chestnut son of New Bay was on the way up for Jane Chapple-Hyam in 2024, adding to a handicap-debut score at Chelmsford City in May of that year with another win in the sphere over York’s extended 10 furlongs 16 days later.

A setback led to 154 days off the track and Primo Lara lost his way, running up a 12-race losing streak for Chapple-Hyam and her Newmarket neighbour Jack Morland before coming good at Wolverhampton at the beginning of last month.

Switching from Morland back to his former trainer, the son of New Bay marked his first attempt at a mile and a half with a defeat of Masterinthewoods on Ascot’s King George VI And Queen Elizabeth undercard last time out.

‌



A 7lb rise to a British Horseracing Authority mark of 86 still leaves Primo Lara 5lb shy of his peak figure and give in the ground should not present a problem. Master Builder was back in business here in May warrants respect, along with Say What You See and Explode.

NEWSBOY’S 1-2-3: 1 PRIMO LARA, 2 MASTER BUILDER, 3 SAY WHAT YOU SEE

View 7 Images John (right) & Thady Gosden train Newsboy's tip (Image: PA)

4.45 British Stallion Studs EBF Convivial Maiden Stakes - LANCASTER TOWER did enough on his racecourse debut at Sandown Park last month to be of definite interest here.

‌



The colt, owned by the King and Queen and trained by John and Thady Gosden, is bred to be smart - he’s by Kingman out of the 2019 Poule d’Essai des Pouliches (French 1,000 Guineas) heroine Castle Lady.

And he must have been showing up on the Newmarket gallops - Lancaster Tower went off the 5-6 favourite to beat five opponents in Esher 23 days ago.

The result of that seven-furlong novice stakes records that my selection finished third, a length and three-quarters behind subsequent Listed winner Quest For Stars.

But Lancaster Tower travelled with menace before his lack of previous experience took its toll, and he’s expected to prove a different proposition at the second time of asking. Oklahoma, Launch Sequence and Speyside have all shown above-average ability in five races between them and are taken to fight it out for the minor medals.

‌



NEWSBOY’S 1-2-3: 1 LANCASTER TOWER, 2 LAUNCH SEQUENCE, 3 SPEYSIDE

View 7 Images Trainer Ed Walker (Image: PA)

5.20 Sky Bet EBF Fillies' Handicap - ELECTRIFARHH looks worth a try at a mile and a quarter and brings untapped potential to the table.

The daughter of Farhh is now four years old but hasn’t had much racing - she has the seventh outing of her career today.

‌



The winner of a novice stakes for fillies at Kempton Park in October 2024, Electrifarhh was limited to just one start last season, finishing second to subsequent Group 1 heroine Blue Bolt at Windsor in May 2025.

The Ed Walker trainee was entitled to need her first outing for 313 days when seventh of nine in a Kempton handicap last March and, while she couldn’t get competitive when sixth to River King at Newbury next time, there was more to like her run over a mile at Glorious Goodwood last time.

Sent off at 18-1 in a field of 14 and wearing the hold that is persevered with today, Electrifarhh and Kieran Shoemark came home with gusto to take third, beaten a nose and three-quarters of a length behind Rumba Numba.

Her finishing effort makes the step up in distance a logical move and a 2lb nudge up the weights should not prevent another decent effort. Janey Mackers, Naga and favourite Silver Lake sit at the top of a lengthy shortlist.

‌



NEWSBOY’S 1-2-3: 1 ELECTRIFARHH, 2 JANEY MACKERS, 3 SILVER LAKE

Sports.title: Kalpana lands Yorkshire Oaks thriller but stablemate Item is team's  'first preference' for Arc
Sports.content:
Kalpana lands Yorkshire Oaks thriller but stablemate Item is team's 'first preference' for Arc

Kalpana just held on to land the Legends Global Yorkshire Oaks at York after a mighty scare from Sparan Nua in a thrilling Group One finish

View 3 Images Kalpana (left) won by a short head (Image: Richard Sellers/PA Wire)

King George heroine survived a late scare to claim the Yorkshire Oaks at York on Thursday. She was all out to thwart the dramatic late challenge of Sparan Nua in the Legends Global Yorkshire Oaks.

‌



The 10-11 favourite was made to work hard for her latest win after Aidan O'Brien's outsider Sugar Island went off in front, pulling into a 20 length lead as the field rounded the home turn.

‌



It was left to Colin Keane to chase her down from 3f out and then pass her, only for Jim Bolger's Sparan Nua – who found herself slightly hampered at one point – to eat up considerable ground and narrow the deficit.

‌



The winning post arrived just in time for Kalpana to prevail by a short head, handing Keane, Andrew Balding and owners Juddmonte a second Group One triumph within 24 hours, following Item's victory in the prestigious Juddmonte International on Wednesday.

"You knew after going a couple of furlongs it was going to be messy and passing the three (furlong marker) I thought the pacemaker was gone," said Juddmonte's European racing manager Barry Mahon.

"Colin had to commit probably a bit sooner than he wanted. When he saw himself the pacemaker was gone he had to chase her down a little bit, so she was always going to be vulnerable to something closing late, but she's gutsy and knows where the line is.

‌



View 3 Images Kalpana with the Juddmonte team at York (Image: Richard Sellers/PA Wire)

"She put her head down and got the job done. It's not pretty, but she got the job done and that's the main thing. Fast ground, slow ground, 12 furlongs - you wouldn't even be afraid to drop her back to 10. She's just very versatile and the ultimate pro now. She's fully matured now at five years of age and keeps answering all the questions, so it's wonderful."

Connections must now consider how to split their aces, with either Kalpana or Item likely to get a shot at the Prix de l'Arc de Triomphe.

‌



Should Item be given the green light to head for ParisLongchamp, Kalpana - who finished seventh in last year's Arc - will almost certainly bid to win the Qipco British Champions Fillies & Mares Stakes at Ascot later in October.

Mahon added: "We have the horse from yesterday too, so whether he'll go to the Arc and we wait for Ascot with this filly - we have to sit down in a week or two and discuss all that, but it's a nice problem to have.

View 3 Images There was a very tight finish to the Yorkshire Oaks (Image: Getty Images)

‌



"The horse from yesterday has joined the fray, so we'll decide all those sort of things in the next couple of weeks with the owners and see what they want to do.

"Item is definitely a top of the ground horse. He got away with the good to soft here yesterday. Funnily enough Colin actually said this filly doesn't enjoy the softer ground as much as she did last year, he said she felt like she enjoyed the faster ground in Ascot more the last time than she did today.

"I wouldn't have thought we'd run both in the Arc. Again that will be the owners' decision, but it wouldn't be my first preference.

Article continues below

"I suppose with Item being a colt, if the ground comes up good he'd probably have the preference, and with this filly Ascot was always the target, so it would make sense to sidestep the Arc if the ground is good - but that's a big `if'.

"She probably will retire at the end of the year. Whether she'll finish at Ascot or if she doesn't go to the Arc whether she'll go to the Breeders' Cup - there's a lot of variables to work out."

Sports.title: Michael Dods seeks 'icing on the cake' with Gimcrack favourite Arapaho Gold
Sports.content:
Michael Dods seeks 'icing on the cake' with Gimcrack favourite Arapaho Gold

In a 36 year career the Darlington trainer has made his name with top level sprinters Mecca’s Angel, Mabs Cross and the veteran Commanche Falls, but now heads to York with an exciting two-year-old

View 3 Images Michael Dods: trains Arapaho Gold (Image: PA)

Michael Dods believes he has a youngster who can serve it up to the big stables at York on Friday.

‌



In a 36-year career the Darlington trainer has made his name with top level sprinters Mecca’s Angel, twice winner of the Nunthorpe Stakes, Prix de l’Abbaye winner Mabs Cross and the veteran Commanche Falls, the only horse this century to win back-to-back Stewards Cups.

‌



While they excelled as older horses, the trainer’s newest protege is two-year-old gelding Arapaho Gold, whose record of three runs undefeated has established him as ante-post favourite for the Group 2 Gimcrack Stakes. “It’s hard to say what we have but he’s an exciting two-year-old who I could see improving over another furlong,” says Dods.

‌



Andrew Balding writes new ending to £1.5m summer blockbuster with unbeaten Item READ MORE :

“But we like having runners at York and the Gimcrack was the obvious race to send him to. There’s some improving horses in there and it’s not going to be an easy race by any means.”

Arapaho Gold, bought for €42,000 as a yearling, won twice at Thirsk before stepping up in class to land the Listed Rose Bowl Stakes at Newbury.

He did it the hard way, having been broadsided after a furlong, to hold off Godolphin challenger Nabati by a neck.

‌



“He was drawn wide, he took a bump early on that set him alight and then he grounded it out and showed a good attitude,” says the trainer.

View 3 Images Mab's Cross (nearest): won the Prix de l'Abbaye (Image: Getty)

“We sort of expected him to win first time out and then we expected him to win at Beverley and then go to Royal Ascot in the Windsor Castle.

‌



“It was probably a blessing that he misbehaved in the stalls at Beverley and was withdrawn. So he didn’t go to Royal Ascot. It might have fried his brains if he’d run there and if he’d been drawn on the wrong side at Ascot it would have been a waste of time. Instead he did the job well at Newbury.”

Arapaho Gold runs in the same colours as Commanche Falls, whose part-owner 82-year-old Doug Graham has been a long time supporter of the Dods stable.

View 3 Images Commanche Falls: won the Coral Stewards' Cup twice (Image: Getty)

‌



Dods said: “Doug’s been involved in Commanche Falls and Dakota Gold so has had a lot of success and it’s nice to get him another good one at his age.

“My wife Carole co-owns Arapaho Gold and works with me and our daughter Chloe is my assistant so it’s nice for some good ones to be coming through for her.

“To win a race like the Gimcrack would be marvellous for everyone involved, Conor Beasley, the staff, the owners and the yard and to win it at York, where we’ve had such a lot of success would be the icing on the cake.”
